knowledge_statements.title: Common-Root Arborescence Packing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Edmonds cut characterization for arc-disjoint spanning out-arborescences with one prescribed root.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\) be a finite digraph, let \(r\in V\), and let \(k\ge 1\). There exist \(k\) pairwise arc-disjoint spanning out-arborescences rooted at \(r\) if and only if \(\lvert\delta_D^-(X)\rvert\ge k\) for every nonempty set \(X\subseteq V\setminus\{r\}\), where \(\delta_D^-(X)\) is the set of arcs entering \(X\) from \(V\setminus X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: There are k arc-disjoint spanning out-arborescences rooted at r exactly when every nonempty set excluding r has at least k entering arcs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists\ k\text{ arc-disjoint spanning }r\text{-out-arborescences}\iff \lvert\delta_D^-(X)\rvert\ge k\quad\forall\varnothing\ne X\subseteq V\setminus\{r\}.\)

notation.meaning: Arcs entering X from its complement.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Arc-disjoint spanning out-arborescences with an ordered, possibly repeated root prescription.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\) be a finite digraph and let \((r_1,\ldots,r_k)\in V^k\), with repetitions allowed. knowledge_statements.title: Designated Root-Set Packings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Packing whose selected roots must belong to a fixed designated vertex set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\), let \(R\subseteq V\), and let \(k\ge 1\). An \(R\)-designated packing of size \(k\) is a family of pairwise arc-disjoint spanning out-arborescences \((T_1,\ldots,T_k)\) together with roots \((r_1,\ldots,r_k)\in R^k\), such that \(T_i\) is rooted at \(r_i\) for every \(i\). knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A designated-root-set packing consists of arc-disjoint spanning arborescences whose chosen roots all lie in a specified vertex set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((T_i,r_i)_{i=1}^k\text{ is designated}\iff r_i\in R\text{ and }T_i\text{ is a spanning }r_i\text{-out-arborescence, pairwise arc-disjoint}.\)

knowledge_statements.title: Flexible Root-Location Packings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Root locations are selected jointly with the arborescences from an admissible family.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\), let \(k\ge 1\), and let \(\mathcal R\subseteq V^k\) be a family of admissible ordered root tuples. A flexible root-location packing is a tuple \(((r_1,\ldots,r_k),T_1,\ldots,T_k)\) such that \((r_1,\ldots,r_k)\in\mathcal R\), each \(T_i\) is a spanning out-arborescence rooted at \(r_i\), and the arc sets \(A(T_1),\ldots,A(T_k)\) are pairwise disjoint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A flexible packing chooses an admissible root tuple and simultaneously packs one spanning out-arborescence from each chosen root.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \((r_1,\ldots,r_k)\in\mathcal R,\quad T_i\text{ is rooted at }r_i,\quad A(T_i)\cap A(T_j)=\varnothing\text{ for }i\ne j.\)

notation.meaning: Family of admissible ordered root tuples.

children.title: Root-Selection Feasibility

knowledge_statements.title: Root-Selection Feasibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cut feasibility condition for selecting an admissible root tuple before packing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\), let \(k\ge1\), and let \(\mathcal R\subseteq V^k\). A flexible root-location packing exists if and only if there is a tuple \((r_1,\ldots,r_k)\in\mathcal R\) such that \(\lvert\delta_D^-(X)\rvert\ge\lvert\{i:r_i\notin X\}\rvert\) for every nonempty \(X\subseteq V\). Thus root selection is feasible precisely when some admissible tuple satisfies all multiple-root cut inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Root selection is feasible exactly when some admissible root tuple satisfies every entering-cut requirement induced by roots outside each set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists\text{ flexible packing}\iff\exists(r_1,\ldots,r_k)\in\mathcal R\;\forall\varnothing\ne X\subseteq V,\ \lvert\delta_D^-(X)\rvert\ge\lvert\{i:r_i\notin X\}\rvert.\)

notation.meaning: Admissible family of root tuples.
Arcs entering X from its complement.

children.title: Capacitated Arborescence Packing
children.top_down_role: Packing with arc capacities or multiplicities.

knowledge_statements.title: Capacitated Arborescence Packing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Integral-capacity extension of the common-root arborescence-packing theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\), let \(r\in V\), let \(k\ge1\), and assign each arc an integral capacity \(u(a)\ge0\). There exist \(k\) spanning out-arborescences rooted at \(r\), with every arc \(a\) used by at most \(u(a)\) members of the family, if and only if \(u(\delta_D^-(X))\ge k\) for every nonempty \(X\subseteq V\setminus\{r\}\), where \(u(F)=\sum_{a\in F}u(a)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A capacitated digraph supports k rooted spanning arborescences exactly when every cut excluding the root has total entering capacity at least k.
assumptions_latex: \(D=(V,A)\) is a finite digraph and \(r\in V\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists\text{ a capacity-respecting family of }k\text{ spanning }r\text{-arborescences}\iff u(\delta_D^-(X))\ge k\quad\forall\varnothing\ne X\subseteq V\setminus\{r\}.\)

notation.meaning: Sum of integral arc capacities over F.
Arcs entering X from its complement.

knowledge_statements.title: Matroid-Based Arborescence Packing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Matroid-basic packing with root labels placed at vertices.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\), let \(S\) be a finite set of root labels, let \(\pi:S\to V\), and let \(M\) be a matroid on \(S\). An \(M\)-basic arborescence packing is a pairwise arc-disjoint family \((T_s:s\in S)\) in which \(T_s\) is an out-arborescence rooted at \(\pi(s)\), and for every \(v\in V\), the set \(\{s\in S:v\in V(T_s)\}\) is a base of \(M\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A matroid-basic packing uses placed root labels and requires the arborescences containing each vertex to be indexed by a matroid base.
assumptions_latex: \(\pi:S\to V\) and \(M\) is a matroid on \(S\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A(T_s)\cap A(T_t)=\varnothing\text{ for }s\ne t,\qquad \{s:v\in V(T_s)\}\text{ is a base of }M\text{ for every }v\in V.\)

notation.meaning: Placement mapping from root labels to vertices.
Matroid governing local coverage by root labels.
Out-arborescence indexed by root label s.

knowledge_statements.title: Directed-Hypergraph Arborescence Packing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Trimming-based definition for packing rooted spanning directed hyperarborescences.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A directed hypergraph has hyperarcs \(e=(T_e,h_e)\) with nonempty tail \(T_e\subseteq V\) and head \(h_e\in V\setminus T_e\). A set \(F\) of hyperarcs is a spanning out-hyperarborescence rooted at \(r\) if one can select \(t_e\in T_e\) for each \(e\in F\) so that the arcs \((t_e,h_e)\) form a spanning out-arborescence rooted at \(r\). A packing is a family of such hyperarborescences having pairwise disjoint hyperarc sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Under the trimming convention, packed hyperarborescences are hyperarc-disjoint families that can each be trimmed to a rooted spanning out-arborescence.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) and the directed-hyperarc family are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\text{ is an }r\text{-hyperarborescence}\iff\exists(t_e\in T_e:e\in F)\text{ whose trimmed arcs form a spanning }r\text{-out-arborescence}.\)

notation.meaning: Tail set of directed hyperarc e.
Head vertex of directed hyperarc e.
Tail vertex selected when trimming e.

knowledge_statements.title: Disjoint Branchings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Edmonds cut characterization for arc-disjoint spanning branchings with prescribed root sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\) be a finite digraph and let \(R_1,\ldots,R_k\) be nonempty subsets of \(V\). There exist pairwise arc-disjoint spanning branchings \(B_1,\ldots,B_k\), with the root set of \(B_i\) equal to \(R_i\), if and only if every nonempty \(X\subseteq V\) satisfies \(\lvert\delta_D^-(X)\rvert\ge\lvert\{i:R_i\cap X=\varnothing\}\rvert\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Prescribed-root-set branchings can be packed exactly when every vertex set receives one entering arc for each branching having no root inside it.
assumptions_latex: \(R_i\subseteq V\) is nonempty for \(1\le i\le k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\exists\text{ arc-disjoint spanning }R_i\text{-branchings }B_i\iff \lvert\delta_D^-(X)\rvert\ge\lvert\{i:R_i\cap X=\varnothing\}\rvert\quad\forall\varnothing\ne X\subseteq V.\)

notation.meaning: Prescribed root set of the i-th branching.
Arcs entering X from its complement.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Edmonds’ Disjoint Branchings Theorem
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cut characterization for packing arc-disjoint branchings with prescribed root sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\) be a digraph and let \(R_1,\ldots,R_k\subseteq V\). There exist pairwise arc-disjoint branchings \(B_1,\ldots,B_k\), with \(B_i\) having root set \(R_i\) for every \(i\), if and only if \[d^{\mathrm{in}}(U)\geq \left|\{i:R_i\cap U=\varnothing\}\right|\] for every nonempty \(U\subseteq V\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A digraph contains pairwise arc-disjoint branchings with prescribed root sets R_i exactly when every nonempty vertex set U has at least one entering arc for each prescribed root set disjoint from U.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists\text{ pairwise arc-disjoint branchings }B_i\text{ rooted at }R_i\ \Longleftrightarrow\ \forall\varnothing\neq U\subseteq V,\ d^{\mathrm{in}}(U)\geq|\{i:R_i\cap U=\varnothing\}|

knowledge_statements.title: Covering by Branchings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Arc covering, with decomposition reserved for pairwise disjoint covering branchings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\) be a finite digraph. A branching cover of \(D\) is a family \(B_1,\ldots,B_k\) of branchings contained in \(D\) such that \(A=\bigcup_{i=1}^k A(B_i)\). Its size is \(k\). It is a branching decomposition when the sets \(A(B_i)\) are pairwise disjoint; equivalently, every arc of \(D\) belongs to exactly one member of the family.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A branching cover contains every arc in at least one branching; it is a decomposition when each arc belongs to exactly one branching.
assumptions_latex: Each \(B_i\) is a branching contained in \(D\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A=\bigcup_{i=1}^k A(B_i),\qquad \text{and for a decomposition }A(B_i)\cap A(B_j)=\varnothing\text{ whenever }i\ne j.\)

notation.meaning: The i-th branching in the cover.
Arc set of branching B_i.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Equitable Covering by Branchings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Balances the cardinalities of the branchings in an arc cover.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let D=(V,A) be a digraph and k\in\mathbb Z_{+}. If A can be covered by k branchings, then there are branchings B_1,\ldots,B_k such that A=\bigcup_{i=1}^{k}B_i and |B_i|\in\{\lfloor |A|/k\rfloor,\lceil |A|/k\rceil\} for every i.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Characterization of arc coverings by k branchings
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives necessary and sufficient vertex-indegree and induced-subgraph sparsity conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \text{Let }D=(V,A)\text{ be a digraph and }k\in\mathbb Z_+.\text{ Then }A\text{ can be covered by }k\text{ branchings if and only if }\deg^{\mathrm{in}}(v)\le k\text{ for every }v\in V\text{ and }|A[U]|\le k(|U|-1)\text{ for every nonempty }U\subseteq V.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The arcs of a digraph can be covered by k branchings exactly when every vertex has indegree at most k and every nonempty vertex set U induces at most k(|U|-1) arcs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A\text{ is coverable by }k\text{ branchings}\iff \bigl(\forall v\in V,\ \deg^{\mathrm{in}}(v)\le k\bigr)\land\bigl(\forall\varnothing\ne U\subseteq V,\ |A[U]|\le k(|U|-1)\bigr).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Root-set reassignment in a two-branching decomposition
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes when arcs partitioned by two branchings can be repartitioned into branchings with prescribed root sets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: \text{Let }B_1,B_2\text{ be branchings partitioning }A\text{ in }D=(V,A).\text{ Let }R_1,R_2\text{ satisfy }R_1\cup R_2=R(B_1)\cup R(B_2)\text{ and }R_1\cap R_2=R(B_1)\cap R(B_2).\text{ Then }A\text{ can be split into branchings }B'_1,B'_2\text{ with }R(B'_i)=R_i\ (i=1,2)\text{ if and only if every strong component }K\text{ of }D\text{ with }d^{\mathrm{in}}(K)=0\text{ intersects both }R_1\text{ and }R_2.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Given a partition of the arcs into two branchings and compatible prescribed root sets, the arcs can be repartitioned into branchings with those root sets exactly when every source strong component meets both prescribed root sets.
assumptions_latex: B_1\text{ and }B_2\text{ are branchings that partition }A.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \bigl(\exists B'_1,B'_2\text{ partitioning }A:\ R(B'_i)=R_i\text{ for }i=1,2\bigr)\iff\bigl(\forall K\text{ a strong component with }d^{\mathrm{in}}(K)=0,\ K\cap R_1\ne\varnothing\text{ and }K\cap R_2\ne\varnothing\bigr).

knowledge_statements.title: Covering by Rooted Arborescences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Arc covering by spanning out-arborescences having a prescribed common root.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\) be a finite digraph and let \(r\in V\). An \(r\)-rooted arborescence cover is a family \(T_1,\ldots,T_k\) of spanning out-arborescences rooted at \(r\) such that \(A=\bigcup_{i=1}^k A(T_i)\). It is an \(r\)-rooted arborescence decomposition when the sets \(A(T_i)\) are pairwise disjoint, so every arc belongs to exactly one rooted arborescence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A rooted-arborescence cover covers every arc by spanning out-arborescences with the prescribed root; a decomposition assigns every arc exactly once.
assumptions_latex: \(D=(V,A)\) is a finite digraph and \(r\in V\).
Each \(T_i\) is a spanning out-arborescence rooted at \(r\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A=\bigcup_{i=1}^k A(T_i),\qquad \text{and for a decomposition }A(T_i)\cap A(T_j)=\varnothing\text{ whenever }i\ne j.\)

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Subset-Rank Criterion for Covering by Rooted Arborescences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes a rooted-arborescence cover using the maximum intersection of one rooted arborescence with each arc subset.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let D=(V,A) be a digraph, r\in V, and k\in\mathbb Z_{+}. For each A'\subseteq A, define s(A')=\max\{|B\cap A'|:B\text{ is an }r\text{-arborescence}\}. Then A can be covered by k r-arborescences if and only if k\,s(A')\geq |A'| for every A'\subseteq A.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: The arcs can be covered by k arborescences rooted at r exactly when, for every arc subset, k times the largest intersection of that subset with one r-arborescence is at least the subset's cardinality.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A\text{ is coverable by }k\ r\text{-arborescences}\iff\forall A'\subseteq A,\ k\,s(A')\geq |A'|

Its weight is \(w^\top x=\sum_{a\in A}w_a x_a\). The arc-disjoint version additionally requires \(x_a\le 1\) for every \(a\in A\).

children.title: Matroid-Partition Packing Algorithms
children.top_down_role: Constructive realization of forest union and tree packing.

assumptions_latex: A finite graph \(G=(V,E)\), an integer \(k\ge 1\), and independence oracles for \(k\) copies of its graphic matroid are given.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm returns a maximum-cardinality union of \(k\) forests; it yields \(k\) edge-disjoint spanning trees exactly when the final size is \(k(|V|-1)\).

notation.meaning: Current partition into independent sets of the k matroid copies.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(I_1=\cdots=I_k=\varnothing\). For the current independent partition, construct the standard matroid-partition exchange digraph \(H_I\): its arcs encode moving an element between parts while preserving independence, and its sources are unused elements insertable into some part. If an augmenting path exists, perform its exchanges and increase \(\sum_i|I_i|\) by one. Otherwise stop and output \((I_1,\ldots,I_k)\). For graphic matroids, each \(I_i\) is a forest; size \(k(|V|-1)\) forces every part to be a spanning tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeated exchange-path augmentations produce a maximum union of k forests; reaching k times the spanning-tree size constructs k edge-disjoint spanning trees.

children.title: Submodular-Flow Formulations
children.top_down_role: Directed packing formulations mediated by submodular flow structure.

assumptions_latex: The ground set \(S\) is finite and \(p:2^S\to\mathbb Z\cup\{-\infty\}\) is crossing supermodular.
Integer lower and upper bounds \(\ell,u\in\mathbb Z^A\) are given on a digraph \(D=(S,A)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Packing feasibility becomes membership in an integral submodular-flow polyhedron and can be optimized by submodular-flow algorithms when its defining oracle is available.

notation.meaning: Net inflow into a vertex subset.
Feasible submodular-flow polyhedron.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(x\in\mathbb R^A\), let \(\varrho_x(X)\) and \(\delta_x(X)\) denote total flow entering and leaving \(X\subseteq S\). The submodular-flow formulation is \[Q(p,\ell,u)=\{x\in\mathbb R^A:\ell\le x\le u,\ \varrho_x(X)-\delta_x(X)\ge p(X)\text{ for every }X\subseteq S\}.\] When a packing model's residual cut requirements define the crossing-supermodular function \(p\), its feasible multiplicity vectors are represented by the corresponding projection or face of \(Q(p,\ell,u)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Packing constraints encoded as crossing-supermodular cut demands form a submodular-flow polyhedron with integral bounds and support oracle-based optimization.

assumptions_latex: The ground set \(E\) is finite and \(f:2^E\to\mathbb Z\) is normalized and submodular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every integer point of \(kB(f)\) decomposes into \(k\) integer base points, providing a packing decomposition.

Base polyhedron of the submodular function f.
k-fold dilation of the base polyhedron.

children.title: Disjoint-Arborescence Complexity Boundary
children.top_down_role: Tractability changes caused by root, spanning, and disjointness variants.

assumptions_latex: Arc costs are rational and the directed input graph is finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Spanning fixed-root packing is polynomially solvable, while replacing spanning by terminal coverage yields an NP-hard optimization problem already for one arborescence.

notation.meaning: Prescribed terminal set in the nonspanning variant.
Number of packed arborescences.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Contrasts spanning arborescence packing with the directed Steiner arborescence variant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a prescribed root \(r\) and integer \(k\), minimum-cost packing of \(k\) arc-disjoint spanning out-arborescences is solvable in polynomial time through branching-packing or equivalent cut-based algorithms. If spanning is replaced by the requirement to reach only a prescribed terminal set \(R\subseteq V\), the case \(k=1\) is the minimum-cost directed Steiner arborescence problem and is NP-hard. Thus preserving the root and disjointness while dropping spanning crosses a tractability boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixed-root spanning arborescence packing is polynomial, but requiring only prescribed terminals becomes the NP-hard directed Steiner arborescence problem even for one tree.
knowledge_statements.title: Disjoint-Arborescence Complexity Boundary

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source is supplied for either the polynomial-time packing claim or the NP-hardness of the directed Steiner variant, so the asserted tractability boundary cannot be admitted.

children.title: Lovász Splitting-Off Theorem Family
children.top_down_role: Classical admissibility and complete-splitting theory for even-degree regimes.

assumptions_latex: The finite undirected multigraph \(G=(V\cup\{s\},E)\) has even degree at \(s\).
For some integer \(k\ge 2\), every two vertices of \(V\) have local edge-connectivity at least \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: All edges incident with \(s\) can be split off in pairs while preserving local edge-connectivity at least \(k\) between every pair of vertices in \(V\).

notation.meaning: Maximum number of edge-disjoint paths between x and y.
Vertex to be eliminated by splitting off.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global \(k\)-edge-connectivity version of Lovász's complete splitting-off theorem.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 8. The splitting-off operation and constructive characterizations p. 250

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Assume \(\lambda_G(x,y)\ge k\) for every distinct \(x,y\in V\) and \(d_G(s)\) is even. Then the edges incident with \(s\) can be partitioned into pairs and successively split off so that, after every operation and in the final graph \(G'\) on \(V\), \(\lambda_{G'}(x,y)\ge k\) holds for all distinct \(x,y\in V\). Loops created by splitting are discarded, while parallel edges are permitted.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: At an even-degree auxiliary vertex, all incident edges can be paired and split off while retaining the prescribed global edge-connectivity among remaining vertices.

knowledge_statements.title: Mader Splitting-Off Theorem Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Local-connectivity admissible-pair form of Mader's undirected splitting-off theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: If no edge incident with \(s\) is a bridge and \(d_G(s)\ne 3\), then there are two incident edges \(su\) and \(sv\) whose splitting-off is admissible: in the resulting multigraph \(G_{u,v}\), \[\lambda_{G_{u,v}}(x,y)=\lambda_G(x,y)\qquad\text{for all distinct }x,y\in V\setminus\{s\}.\] The operation deletes \(su,sv\), adds an edge \(uv\), permits parallel edges, and discards the added edge when \(u=v\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unless the distinguished vertex has degree three or an incident bridge, some incident pair can be split without changing any remaining pairwise edge-connectivity.
assumptions_latex: The finite undirected multigraph \(G=(V,E)\) has a vertex \(s\) incident with no bridge.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Some pair of edges incident with \(s\) is admissible for all local edge-connectivities among vertices other than \(s\).

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A complete splitting-off eliminates every edge incident with \(s\), after which the isolated vertex \(s\) may be deleted.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Splitting off a pair \(su,sv\) at \(s\) deletes those two edges and adds one edge \(uv\), with parallel edges allowed and a resulting loop discardable. A complete splitting-off at \(s\) is a sequence of exactly \(d_G(s)/2\) such operations, each using two currently incident edges, whose final graph has \(d(s)=0\). If every operation preserves a specified connectivity requirement on \(V\setminus\{s\}\), the sequence is complete and admissible for that requirement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complete splitting-off pairs and replaces all edges incident with an even-degree vertex until that vertex becomes isolated, optionally preserving a stated connectivity requirement.

knowledge_statements.title: Partial Splitting-Off
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines a prescribed noncomplete elimination extent, independently of any admissibility condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A partial splitting-off of extent \(q\) at \(s\) is a sequence of \(q\) operations, each deleting two currently incident edges \(su,sv\) and adding an edge \(uv\). The resulting graph \(G'\) satisfies \(d_{G'}(s)=d_G(s)-2q>0\). The sequence is admissible relative to a specified family of vertex pairs if every required local edge-connectivity is unchanged after the sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partial splitting-off replaces a positive number of incident edge pairs but leaves the distinguished vertex with positive degree, reducing its degree by twice the number of operations.
assumptions_latex: The finite undirected multigraph \(G=(V,E)\) has a distinguished vertex \(s\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A partial splitting-off performs exactly \(q\) pair operations and leaves positive degree \(d_G(s)-2q\) at \(s\).

children.title: Elimination-Extent Regimes

knowledge_statements.title: Elimination-Extent Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classifies undirected splitting-off sequences by how much of the incidence at the split vertex is eliminated.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be an undirected multigraph and let \(s\in V\). Splitting the pair \(su,sv\) deletes these two edge copies and adds one copy of \(uv\), with a loop allowed when \(u=v\). A splitting-off sequence at \(s\) is partial if it performs any feasible number of such operations. It is complete if its pairs partition all edge copies incident with \(s\), so the resulting graph has \(d(s)=0\) and may be identified with a graph on \(V\setminus\{s\}\). Thus complete elimination is possible only when the initial degree \(d_G(s)\) is even.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Partial splitting removes selected incident-edge pairs; complete splitting pairs every edge at the chosen vertex and therefore requires even degree.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_G(s)\) even is necessary for complete splitting at \(s\).

notation.meaning: Degree of the split vertex, counting multiplicity.

children.title: Blocking-Cut Obstructions
children.top_down_role: Cut configurations that block candidate splitting pairs.

knowledge_statements.title: Blocking-Cut Obstructions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A cut certificate showing that a proposed undirected split violates a prescribed connectivity requirement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\), let \(s\in V\), and prescribe an integer cut requirement \(r(X)\) for each \(X\subseteq V\setminus\{s\}\). Assume \(d_G(X)\ge r(X)\). A set \(X\) blocks the pair \(su,sv\) if \(u,v\in X\) and \(d_G(X)-2<r(X)\). Indeed, splitting \(su,sv\) decreases \(d_G(X)\) by exactly two when both endpoints lie in \(X\), and leaves it unchanged when at most one does. Consequently, the displayed inequalities provide a directly checkable certificate that the pair is inadmissible for preserving all prescribed cut requirements.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A cut containing both split endpoints blocks the pair when losing two crossing edges would make its prescribed connectivity inequality fail.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(u,v\in X\) and \(d_G(X)-2<r(X)\) certify inadmissibility of \(su,sv\).

notation.meaning: Number of edges with exactly one endpoint in the set.
Required lower bound for the cut of the set.

children.title: Dangerous-Set Obstructions
children.top_down_role: Dangerous vertex-set structures restricting splitting admissibility.

knowledge_statements.title: Dangerous-Set Obstructions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uses the standard uniform edge-connectivity specialization of an undirected blocking set.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be an undirected multigraph, let \(s\in V\), and suppose \(d_G(X)\ge k\) for every nonempty proper \(X\subset V\setminus\{s\}\). For a proposed split of \(su,sv\), a nonempty proper set \(X\subset V\setminus\{s\}\) is dangerous for the pair if \(u,v\in X\) and \(d_G(X)\le k+1\). Since the split changes this cut value to \(d_G(X)-2<k\), every dangerous set obstructs preservation of \(k\)-edge-connectivity among the vertices other than \(s\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A dangerous set contains both split endpoints and has cut size at most one above the required connectivity, so splitting violates the requirement.
assumptions_latex: Every relevant cut initially has size at least \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A dangerous set for \(su,sv\) certifies that the pair is not \(k\)-connectivity-preserving.

notation.meaning: Size of the undirected edge boundary of the set.

children.title: Parity Obstructions
children.top_down_role: Parity-sensitive barriers to complete or admissible splitting-off.

knowledge_statements.title: Parity Obstructions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The elementary parity boundary for eliminating every edge incident with an undirected split vertex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Each undirected splitting-off operation at \(s\) removes exactly two edge copies incident with \(s\), and hence preserves the parity of \(d_G(s)\). Therefore a sequence can eliminate all incidence at \(s\) only if \(d_G(s)\) is even. In particular, every multigraph with odd \(d_G(s)\)—for example, a three-edge star centered at \(s\)—admits no complete splitting-off at \(s\), irrespective of which pairs are locally admissible. Partial splitting may terminate with one unpaired edge.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Because every split removes two incident edges, odd degree prevents complete elimination and leaves at least one edge unpaired.
assumptions_latex: A split always consumes two edge copies incident with \(s\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(d_G(s)\equiv 1\pmod 2\) implies that complete splitting-off at \(s\) is impossible.

notation.meaning: Degree at the split vertex, counting multiplicity.

children.title: Directed Splitting-Off
children.top_down_role: Incoming–outgoing arc-pair reductions preserving directed connectivity.

children.title: Directed Splitting-Off Theorem Families
children.top_down_role: Existence and admissibility theory for directed local reductions.

knowledge_statements.title: Directed Splitting-Off Theorem Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Common framework underlying directed existence and admissibility theorems, without selecting one theorem’s specialized hypotheses.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a directed multigraph \(D=(V,A)\) and \(s\in V\), splitting the consecutive pair \(us,sv\) deletes those arc copies and adds \(uv\). Directed splitting-off theorems seek a pair, or a sequence of pairs, for which specified connectivities between vertices of \(V\setminus\{s\}\) remain unchanged. Their hypotheses typically combine cut lower bounds, balance or degree conditions at \(s\), and exclusion of exceptional configurations; their conclusions distinguish existence of one admissible pair from existence of a complete admissible splitting. These conclusions are logically distinct because local admissibility need not supply a pairing of every arc at \(s\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Directed splitting theorems separate existence of one connectivity-preserving in-arc/out-arc pair from existence of a complete pairing at the eliminated vertex.
assumptions_latex: The split pairs an arc entering \(s\) with an arc leaving \(s\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Existence of one admissible pair and existence of a complete admissible splitting are separate theorem regimes.

notation.meaning: An arc entering and an arc leaving the split vertex.
Replacement arc created by the directed split.

children.title: Directed Splitting Elimination-Extent Regimes
children.top_down_role: Full and selective elimination by incoming–outgoing arc pairings.

children.title: Complete Directed Splitting
children.top_down_role: Directed splitting regimes aimed at full vertex elimination.

knowledge_statements.title: Complete Directed Splitting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines complete directed elimination through a pairing of all arcs incident with the split vertex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\) be a directed multigraph and let \(s\in V\). A complete directed splitting at \(s\) is determined by a bijection between the arc copies entering \(s\) and those leaving \(s\). For every matched pair \(us,sv\), delete the two arcs and add \(uv\). After all matched pairs are split, no arc is incident with \(s\), and \(s\) may be deleted. Such a complete pairing exists only if \(d_D^-(s)=d_D^+(s)\); connectivity-preserving completeness additionally requires every split in the chosen sequence to satisfy the stipulated admissibility condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complete directed splitting pairs every entering arc with one leaving arc, requiring equal indegree and outdegree and admissibility throughout the sequence.
assumptions_latex: Arc copies are distinguished when parallel arcs occur.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Complete directed splitting requires \(d_D^-(s)=d_D^+(s)\).

notation.meaning: Indegree of the split vertex.
Outdegree of the split vertex.

children.title: Partial Directed Splitting
children.top_down_role: Selective directed splitting with residual incident arcs.

knowledge_statements.title: Partial Directed Splitting
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines proper partial directed splitting that consumes selected entering and leaving arcs but does not eliminate all incidence at the split vertex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\) be a finite directed multigraph and let \(s\in V\). A proper partial directed splitting at \(s\) chooses equally large nonempty subsets \(I'\subseteq\delta_D^-(s)\) and \(O'\subseteq\delta_D^+(s)\), together with a bijection from \(I'\) to \(O'\), such that at least one arc incident with \(s\) is unchosen. Each matched pair \(us,sv\) is replaced by \(uv\), while all unchosen arcs remain incident with \(s\). Connectivity-preserving partial splitting additionally requires each pair to be admissible when it is split in the resulting sequence.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A proper partial directed splitting pairs a nonempty selection of entering and leaving arcs while leaving at least one incident arc at the split vertex.
assumptions_latex: Arc copies are distinguished when parallel arcs occur.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: After splitting \(|I'|\) pairs, \(d_D^-(s)-|I'|\) entering arcs and \(d_D^+(s)-|I'|\) leaving arcs remain, with at least one of these two numbers positive.

notation.meaning: Set of arc copies entering the split vertex.
Set of arc copies leaving the split vertex.
Selected entering and leaving arc copies.

children.title: Arc-Pairing Feasibility Regimes
children.top_down_role: Structural regimes governing usable incoming–outgoing arc pairings.

knowledge_statements.title: Arc-Pairing Feasibility Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates cardinality feasibility of directed arc pairing from connectivity-preserving admissibility.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\) be a finite directed multigraph, let \(s\in V\), and let \(q\) be a nonnegative integer. Exactly \(q\) directed splits can be specified using distinct arc copies precisely when there are subsets \(I'\subseteq\delta_D^-(s)\) and \(O'\subseteq\delta_D^+(s)\) with \(|I'|=|O'|=q\), together with a bijection between them. Thus cardinality feasibility is equivalent to \(0\le q\le\min\{d_D^-(s),d_D^+(s)\}\). Complete elimination is cardinality-feasible precisely when \(d_D^-(s)=d_D^+(s)=q\). If connectivity must also be preserved, the selected pairs must admit an ordering in which each pair is admissible in the current residual digraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a nonnegative integer q, q pairs are cardinality-feasible exactly when q does not exceed either incident semidegree; complete pairing requires balance, and connectivity preservation imposes sequential admissibility.
assumptions_latex: Each split uses one entering and one leaving arc copy.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(q\) pairs are cardinality-feasible if and only if \(0\le q\le\min\{d_D^-(s),d_D^+(s)\}\).

notation.meaning: Number of directed arc pairs to be split.

children.title: Directed Splitting Admissibility Boundary

children.title: Directed-Cut Obstructions
children.top_down_role: Directed cut configurations that prevent connectivity-preserving splitting.

knowledge_statements.title: Directed-Cut Obstructions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A tight in-cut certificate obstructing a directed split under uniform strong edge-connectivity requirements.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\) be a directed multigraph, let \(s\in V\), and suppose every nonempty proper \(X\subset V\setminus\{s\}\) satisfies \(\rho_D(X)\ge k\). For the proposed split of \(us,sv\), the value \(\rho_D(X)\) decreases by one exactly when \(u,v\in X\); otherwise it is unchanged. Consequently, a nonempty proper set \(X\subset V\setminus\{s\}\) with \(u,v\in X\) and \(\rho_D(X)=k\) is a directed-cut obstruction: after the split its entering cut has size \(k-1\), certifying failure to preserve strong \(k\)-edge-connectivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A tight entering cut containing both external endpoints loses one arc under the directed split and certifies inadmissibility.
assumptions_latex: Every relevant entering cut initially has size at least \(k\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(u,v\in X\) and \(\rho_D(X)=k\) certify that splitting \(us,sv\) violates the cut requirement.

notation.meaning: Number of arcs entering the set from its complement.
Required strong edge-connectivity level.

children.title: Admissible Splitting Pairs
children.top_down_role: Structural classes of arc pairs compatible with preserved connectivity.

knowledge_statements.title: Admissible Splitting Pairs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines directed admissibility by preservation of all local arc-connectivities away from the split vertex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\), let \(s\in V\), and let \(D'\) result from replacing \(us,sv\) by \(uv\). The pair \((us,sv)\) is admissible at \(s\) if, for every ordered pair of distinct vertices \(x,y\in V\setminus\{s\}\), one has \(\lambda_{D'}(x,y)=\lambda_D(x,y)\), where \(\lambda_D(x,y)\) is the maximum number of pairwise arc-disjoint directed paths from \(x\) to \(y\). Relative to a specified demand family, admissibility may instead require equality only for the designated ordered pairs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A directed pair is admissible when replacing its two arcs by the shortcut arc preserves every required ordered-pair arc-connectivity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Admissibility means \(\lambda_{D'}(x,y)=\lambda_D(x,y)\) for every required ordered pair \((x,y)\).

notation.meaning: Digraph obtained after the proposed directed split.
Maximum number of arc-disjoint directed paths from \(x\) to \(y\).

children.title: Obstruction–Admissibility Boundary
children.top_down_role: Boundary cases separating blocked pairings from admissible pairings.

knowledge_statements.title: Obstruction–Admissibility Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cut characterization of admissibility for one directed split under a uniform strong-connectivity requirement.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\) be a finite directed multigraph, let \(s\in V\), and suppose \(\rho_D(X)\ge k\) for every nonempty proper \(X\subset V\setminus\{s\}\). Let \(D'\) arise by splitting \(us,sv\) into \(uv\). Then \(D'\) satisfies the same cut inequalities if and only if there is no nonempty proper \(X\subset V\setminus\{s\}\) such that \(u,v\in X\) and \(\rho_D(X)=k\). Equivalently, the proposed pair is admissible for the uniform cut requirement exactly when \(\rho_D(X)\ge k+1\) for every such set containing both external endpoints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A directed split preserves the uniform cut requirement exactly when no tight entering cut contains both external endpoints of the split.
assumptions_latex: \(\rho_D(X)\ge k\) holds for every relevant nontrivial set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D'\) preserves all level-\(k\) cut inequalities if and only if \(\rho_D(X)\ge k+1\) whenever \(X\) is relevant and \(u,v\in X\).

notation.meaning: Number of arcs entering the set.
Digraph after splitting \(us,sv\) into \(uv\).

children.title: Directed Connectivity Preservation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Directed splitting under root-centered and terminal-pair connectivity targets.

children.title: Rooted Connectivity Preservation
children.top_down_role: Directed splitting under connectivity requirements centered at a distinguished root.

knowledge_statements.title: Rooted Connectivity Preservation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Preservation criterion for directed connectivities to and from a fixed root outside the split vertex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\) be a finite directed multigraph, choose distinct vertices \(r,s\in V\), and let \(D'\) be obtained by replacing \(as,sb\) with \(ab\). The split preserves two-sided rooted local connectivity at \(r\) if, for every \(t\in V\setminus\{r,s\}\), both \(\lambda_{D'}(r,t)=\lambda_D(r,t)\) and \(\lambda_{D'}(t,r)=\lambda_D(t,r)\). Equivalently, for every such \(t\), no minimum entering cut \(X\) with \(t\in X\) and \(r\notin X\), and no minimum entering cut \(X\) with \(r\in X\) and \(t\notin X\), contains both \(a\) and \(b\). For a one-sided rooted requirement, retain only the corresponding equality and cut condition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A directed split preserves two-sided rooted connectivity when every connectivity from the root to a surviving vertex and back remains unchanged; equivalently, no corresponding minimum entering cut contains both external endpoints of the split.
assumptions_latex: The root \(r\) is distinct from the split vertex \(s\).
The proposed directed split replaces \(as,sb\) with \(ab\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Rooted preservation holds exactly when the two displayed connectivity equalities hold for every \(t\in V\setminus\{r,s\}\), equivalently when none of the specified minimum entering cuts contains both \(a\) and \(b\).

notation.meaning: Designated root vertex.
External tail and head of the proposed directed split.
Digraph after the directed split.
Directed local arc-connectivity from \(x\) to \(y\).

children.title: Pairwise Connectivity Preservation
children.top_down_role: Directed splitting under prescribed ordered-pair connectivity requirements.

assumptions_latex: \(D=(V,A)\) is a finite directed multigraph and \(s\in V\).
The split replaces distinct arcs \(xs,sy\in A\) by one arc \(xy\), with multiplicities retained.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda_{D'}(u,v)=\lambda_D(u,v)\) for every ordered pair of distinct vertices \(u,v\in V\setminus\{s\}\).

notation.meaning: maximum number of pairwise arc-disjoint directed paths from u to v
digraph obtained after splitting off xs and sy at s

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact preservation of all ordered local connectivities away from the eliminated vertex.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 8. The splitting-off operation and constructive characterizations p. 250

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D'\) be obtained from \(D\) by splitting off \(xs,sy\) at \(s\). The split is pairwise-connectivity preserving on \(V\setminus\{s\}\) precisely when
\[
\lambda_{D'}(u,v)=\lambda_D(u,v)\qquad\text{for all distinct }u,v\in V\setminus\{s\}.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A directed split at s is pairwise preserving when it leaves unchanged the maximum number of arc-disjoint paths for every ordered pair of remaining vertices.

children.title: Terminal-Specific Preservation
children.top_down_role: Preservation regimes restricted to designated terminal collections.

assumptions_latex: \(D=(V,A)\) is a finite directed multigraph, \(s\in V\), and \(T\subseteq V\setminus\{s\}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\lambda_{D'}(u,v)=\lambda_D(u,v)\) for all distinct \(u,v\in T\).

notation.meaning: designated terminal set
maximum number of arc-disjoint directed u-to-v paths

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Preservation is required only between designated terminals, not all surviving vertices.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 8. The splitting-off operation and constructive characterizations p. 250

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The split of \(xs,sy\) at \(s\) is terminal-specific connectivity preserving for \(T\) when
\[
\lambda_{D'}(u,v)=\lambda_D(u,v)\qquad\text{for every ordered pair of distinct }u,v\in T.
\]
More generally, for prescribed requirements \(r:T\times T\to\mathbb Z_{\geq0}\), it is requirement preserving when \(\lambda_{D'}(u,v)\geq r(u,v)\) for all distinct \(u,v\in T\), assuming \(D\) initially satisfies these inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A split is terminal-specific preserving when all directed connectivity values, or all prescribed lower bounds, remain valid between designated terminals.
knowledge_statements.title: Terminal-Specific Preservation

children.title: Constructive Connectivity Characterizations
children.top_down_role: Reduction-based derivations of connectivity structures.

assumptions_latex: \(G_0=G\) is a finite multigraph with a distinguished auxiliary vertex \(s\).
For each nonterminal \(G_i\), an admissible split produces \(G_{i+1}\), strictly decreases the degree of \(s\), and satisfies \(\mathcal P(G_i)\iff\mathcal P(G_{i+1})\).
The process terminates at a graph \(G_m\) in a specified family of base instances.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal P(G)\iff\mathcal P(G_m)\).

notation.meaning: connectivity predicate preserved by the reductions
graph after i admissible splitting-off operations

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Conditional reduction principle for deriving constructive characterizations from admissible elimination and explicitly specified inverse operations.

source_refs.locator: 8.3 Further constructive characterizations p. 265

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G_0=G\). Suppose every nonterminal \(G_i\) admits a splitting-off operation producing \(G_{i+1}\), strictly decreasing the degree of \(s\), and satisfying
\[
\mathcal P(G_i)\iff\mathcal P(G_{i+1}).
\]
If the sequence terminates at a specified base instance \(G_m\), then
\[
\mathcal P(G)f\mathcal P(G_m).
\]
When the permitted inverse operations are specified and preserve membership in the characterized family, the base instances and those inverse operations give a constructive characterization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sequence of admissible splits that strictly reduces the auxiliary vertex and preserves a connectivity predicate reduces membership to a specified base instance. Specified inverse operations can then furnish a constructive characterization when they preserve the characterized family.

children.title: Path-Packing Reductions
children.top_down_role: Connections between local reductions and path-packing structures.

assumptions_latex: \(D_0,D_1,\ldots,D_m\) is a recorded sequence of finite directed multigraphs in which \(D_i\) is obtained from \(D_{i-1}\) by replacing distinct arcs \(x_is_i,s_iy_i\) with a labeled shortcut arc \(x_iy_i\).
\(\mathcal Q'\) is a family of pairwise arc-disjoint directed paths in \(D_m\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Reverse expansion produces a family \(\mathcal Q\) of pairwise arc-disjoint directed paths in \(D_0\) with \(|\mathcal Q|=|\mathcal Q'|\) and the same corresponding endpoints.

notation.meaning: reduced path family in the final digraph
lifted path family in the original digraph
digraph after i recorded splitting-off operations

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algorithm for lifting an arc-disjoint path packing by reversing labeled local shortcut operations.

source_refs.locator: Chapter 8. The splitting-off operation and constructive characterizations p. 250

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Input the recorded sequence \(D_0,D_1,\ldots,D_m\) and an arc-disjoint path family \(\mathcal Q'\) in \(D_m\). For \(i=m,m-1,\ldots,1\), replace every occurrence of the labeled shortcut arc \(x_iy_i\) created at step \(i\) by the two-arc segment \(x_is_iy_i\). Output the resulting family \(\mathcal Q\) in \(D_0\). The output is arc-disjoint, has the same corresponding endpoints, and satisfies
\[
|\mathcal Q|=|\mathcal Q'|.
\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Process the recorded splits in reverse order, replacing each labeled shortcut arc used by a path with its original two-arc segment. The lifted path family is arc-disjoint and has the same size and corresponding endpoints.
knowledge_statements.title: Path-Packing Reductions

children.title: Connectivity-Augmentation Reductions
children.top_down_role: Use of splitting-off in constructive augmentation theory.

assumptions_latex: An augmentation instance is encoded by an auxiliary vertex \(s\) whose incident stubs represent available edge ends.
Every split used at \(s\) preserves the required connectivity inequalities on the original vertex set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Eliminating \(s\) converts paired stubs into augmenting edges and preserves feasibility of the encoded augmentation instance.

notation.meaning: original graph or digraph
augmentation edges created by splitting off at s

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Auxiliary stubs are paired into augmentation edges while required connectivities remain invariant.

source_refs.locator: 11.1 Augmenting edge-connectivity of undirected graphs p. 373
11.2 Augmenting edge-connectivity of directed graphs p. 383

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent each available augmentation end at \(v\in V(G)\) by an edge or arc incident with a new vertex \(s\). Pair compatible ends by admissible splitting at \(s\); a paired pair at \(u,v\) becomes an augmenting edge or arc joining \(u\) and \(v\). If all required cut or local-connectivity lower bounds are preserved at every split, elimination of \(s\) yields an augmentation set \(F\) such that \(G+F\) satisfies exactly those retained requirements. Reversing the splits recovers the auxiliary representation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Encode augmentation endpoints as stubs at an auxiliary vertex, then split admissible pairs into actual augmentation edges while preserving the required connectivity bounds.
knowledge_statements.title: Connectivity-Augmentation Reductions

source_witnesses.locator: 11.1 Augmenting edge-connectivity of undirected graphs p. 373

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record blends undirected edges, directed arcs, cut requirements, and local-connectivity requirements into one principle without specifying compatibility, parity, orientation, or the hypotheses ensuring complete elimination of the auxiliary vertex. Those details materially affect feasibility, so the cited augmentation sections must be inspected before a reliable mathematical version can be selected.

children.title: Network Synthesis Reductions
children.top_down_role: Realization and synthesis uses of connectivity-preserving elimination.

assumptions_latex: The total degree \(d(V)=\sum_{v\in V}d(v)\) is even and \(2d(v)\leq d(V)\) for every \(v\in V\).
The hub multigraph \(H\) has vertex set \(V\cup\{s\}\) and exactly \(d(v)\) parallel edges between \(s\) and each \(v\in V\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The hub edges can be completely paired at distinct vertices and split off to produce a loopless multigraph \(G\) on \(V\) satisfying \(\deg_G(v)=d(v)\) for every \(v\in V\).

notation.meaning: prescribed degree of vertex v
sum of the prescribed degrees over V
auxiliary hub vertex
hub multigraph encoding the prescribed edge ends

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hub elimination represents loopless multigraph synthesis as pairing prescribed endpoint stubs; connectivity constraints require an additionally admissible complete pairing.

source_refs.locator: 8.3 Further constructive characterizations p. 265

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Form the hub multigraph \(H\) on \(V\cup\{s\}\) with exactly \(d(v)\) copies of \(sv\) for each \(v\in V\). If \(d(V)\) is even and \(2d(v)\leq d(V)\) for every \(v\in V\), the hub edges can be paired so that the two edges in each pair have distinct endpoints in \(V\). Replacing every paired \(su,sv\) by \(uv\) yields a loopless multigraph \(G\) satisfying
\[
\deg_G(v)=d(v)\qquad\text{for every }v\in V.
\]
If the complete pairing is also admissible for specified connectivity requirements, the resulting graph realizes those requirements as well.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Encode the prescribed degrees as stubs incident with a hub. An even degree sum and no vertex demanding more than all other vertices combined permit complete pairing at distinct endpoints, producing a loopless multigraph with the prescribed degrees. Additional connectivity requirements are retained only when the complete pairing is admissible for them.
knowledge_statements.title: Network Synthesis Reductions

children.title: Nash-Williams Orientation Theorem Family
children.top_down_role: Higher-connectivity orientation theory for undirected graphs.

assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is a finite undirected multigraph and \(k\in\mathbb Z_{\geq1}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G\) has a \(k\)-arc-connected orientation if and only if every nontrivial undirected cut has at least \(2k\) edges.

notation.meaning: undirected edge cut determined by X
directed local arc-connectivity from u to v

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
There exists an orientation \(D\) of \(G\) satisfying
\[
\lambda_D(u,v)\geq k\qquad\text{for every ordered pair of distinct }u,v\in V
\]
if and only if
\[
|\delta_G(X)|\geq 2k\qquad\text{for every nonempty proper subset }X\subset V.
\]
Equivalently, an undirected multigraph has a \(k\)-arc-connected orientation exactly when it is \(2k\)-edge-connected.

assumptions_latex: \(D=(V,A)\) is a finite digraph and \(k\in\mathbb Z_{\geq1}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D\) is \(k\)-arc-connected exactly when every nonempty proper vertex set has at least \(k\) entering arcs and at least \(k\) leaving arcs.

notation.meaning: number of arcs entering X from its complement
number of arcs leaving X toward its complement
maximum number of pairwise arc-disjoint directed paths from u to v

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The digraph \(D\) is \(k\)-arc-connected when
\[
\lambda_D(u,v)\geq k\qquad\text{for every ordered pair of distinct }u,v\in V.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
\rho_D(X)\geq k\quad\text{and}\quad\delta_D(X)\geq k
\qquad\text{for every nonempty proper }X\subset V.
\]
Either the entering-cut inequalities or the leaving-cut inequalities, when imposed over all nonempty proper subsets, is an equivalent cut formulation.

Equivalently, every nontrivial vertex subset has at least k entering arcs and at least k leaving arcs; either cut family over all nontrivial subsets suffices.

children.title: Rooted Edge-Connected Orientations
children.top_down_role: Orientations satisfying root-centered directed connectivity.

assumptions_latex: \(D=(V,A)\) is a finite digraph, \(r\in V\), and \(k\in\mathbb Z_{\geq1}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D\) is outwardly rooted \(k\)-edge-connected at \(r\) exactly when \(\rho_D(X)\geq k\) for every nonempty \(X\subseteq V\setminus\{r\}\).

notation.meaning: designated root
number of arcs entering X
maximum number of pairwise arc-disjoint directed paths from u to v

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Outward root-to-vertex convention; the inward version reverses all arcs.

source_refs.locator: 9.1 Rooted k-edge-connected orientations and reorientations p. 285

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The digraph \(D\) is outwardly rooted \(k\)-edge-connected with root \(r\) if
\[
\lambda_D(r,v)\geq k\qquad\text{for every }v\in V\setminus\{r\}.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
\rho_D(X)\geq k\qquad\text{for every nonempty }X\subseteq V\setminus\{r\}.
\]
The inwardly rooted convention requires \(\lambda_D(v,r)\geq k\) for every \(v\in V\setminus\{r\}\), equivalently \(\delta_D(X)\geq k\) for every nonempty \(X\subseteq V\setminus\{r\}\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An outwardly rooted k-edge-connected digraph has k arc-disjoint directed paths from the root to every other vertex, equivalently at least k arcs enter every nonempty root-free set. The inward convention reverses the path directions and uses leaving cuts.

assumptions_latex: \(D=(V,A)\) is a finite digraph and \(k\in\mathbb Z_{\geq1}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D\) is globally \(k\)-edge-connected when \(\lambda_D(u,v)\geq k\) for every ordered pair of distinct vertices.

number of arcs entering X

The digraph \(D\) is globally \(k\)-edge-connected, also called \(k\)-arc-connected, if

\lambda_D(u,v)\geq k\qquad\text{for all distinct }u,v\in V.
\]
Equivalently,
\[
\rho_D(X)\geq k\qquad\text{for every nonempty proper subset }X\subset V.
\]
An orientation of an undirected graph is a global \(k\)-edge-connected orientation when its resulting digraph satisfies these equivalent conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A digraph is globally k-edge-connected when every ordered pair has k arc-disjoint directed paths, equivalently every nontrivial set has at least k entering arcs.

children.title: Root-Centered Connectivity Requirements
children.top_down_role: Connectivity targets measured relative to a distinguished root.

assumptions_latex: \(D=(V,A)\) is a finite digraph with root \(r\in V\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The root-centered \((k,\ell)\) requirements are equivalent to \(\rho_D(X)\geq k\) and \(\delta_D(X)\geq\ell\) for every nonempty \(X\subseteq V\setminus\{r\}\).

notation.meaning: number of arcs entering X
number of arcs leaving X
directed local arc-connectivity

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asymmetric outward and inward connectivity requirements centered at one root.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The root-centered \((k,\ell)\)-connectivity requirements at \(r\) are
\[
\lambda_D(r,v)\geq k\quad\text{and}\quad\lambda_D(v,r)\geq\ell
\qquad(v\in V\setminus\{r\}).
\]
By directed cut characterizations, these hold exactly when
\[
\rho_D(X)\geq k\quad\text{and}\quad\delta_D(X)\geq\ell
\qquad\text{for every nonempty }X\subseteq V\setminus\{r\}.
\]
The parameters may differ, so outward and inward root connectivity are independently prescribed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Root-centered (k,l) connectivity requires k arc-disjoint paths from the root to every vertex and l in the reverse direction, equivalently corresponding cut inequalities.

children.title: Global Connectivity Requirements
children.top_down_role: Connectivity targets imposed across the full oriented graph.

assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is a finite undirected multigraph without loops.
\(k\in\mathbb Z_{\ge 0}\), and \(D\) is an orientation of \(G\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D\) is globally \(k\)-arc-connected exactly when \(\rho_D(X)\ge k\) for every \(\varnothing\ne X\subsetneq V\).

notation.meaning: Number of arcs entering a vertex set X in D.
Number of arcs leaving a vertex set X in D.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cut formulation of global arc-connectivity for orientations of finite multigraphs.

source_refs.locator: 1.2 Cut functions and connectivity concepts p. 19

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For \(X\subseteq V\), let \(\rho_D(X)\) count arcs with tail in \(V\setminus X\) and head in \(X\), and let \(\delta_D(X)\) count arcs with tail in \(X\) and head in \(V\setminus X\). The orientation \(D\) satisfies the global \(k\)-connectivity requirement if
\[\rho_D(X)\ge k\qquad(\varnothing\ne X\subsetneq V).\]
Since \(\delta_D(X)=\rho_D(V\setminus X)\), this is equivalent to requiring both \(\rho_D(X)\ge k\) and \(\delta_D(X)\ge k\) for every nonempty proper \(X\subset V\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every nontrivial vertex cut must have at least k oriented edges entering it, equivalently at least k arcs in each direction across the cut.
knowledge_statements.title: Global Connectivity Requirements

source_witnesses.locator: 1.2 Cut functions and connectivity concepts p. 19

children.title: Mixed (k,ℓ)-Orientation Regimes
children.top_down_role: Parameter regimes combining root-centered and global orientation requirements.

assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is a finite undirected multigraph, \(r\in V\), and \(D\) is an orientation of \(G\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The mixed rooted requirement is \(\rho_D(X)\ge k\) when \(r\notin X\) and \(\rho_D(X)\ge\ell\) when \(r\in X\), for every nonempty proper \(X\subset V\).

notation.meaning: Distinguished root vertex.
Number of arcs of D entering X.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Root-separated cut interpretation of a mixed \((k,\ell)\)-orientation regime.

source_refs.locator: 9.1 Rooted k-edge-connected orientations and reorientations p. 285

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A rooted orientation \((D,r)\) satisfies the mixed \((k,\ell)\)-connectivity regime when every nonempty proper set obeys
\[\rho_D(X)\ge
\begin{cases}
k,&r\notin X,\\
\ell,&r\in X.
\end{cases}\]
Equivalently, every cut separating \(r\) from \(X\subseteq V\setminus\{r\}\) has at least \(k\) arcs directed from the root side toward \(X\) and at least \(\ell\) arcs directed from \(X\) toward the root side. Thus \(k\) and \(\ell\) independently control the two directions of rooted cut connectivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Across every root-separating cut, at least k arcs point away from the root side and at least ell point toward it.
knowledge_statements.title: Mixed (k,ℓ)-Orientation Regimes

source_witnesses.locator: 9.1 Rooted k-edge-connected orientations and reorientations p. 285

children.title: Asymmetric Directional Requirements
children.top_down_role: Orientation regimes with unequal connectivity requirements in opposite directions.

assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is a finite undirected multigraph and \(D\) is an orientation of \(G\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(D\) meets the directional requirements exactly when \(\rho_D(X)\ge p(X)\) and \(\delta_D(X)\ge q(X)\) for every \(\varnothing\ne X\subsetneq V\).

notation.meaning: Numbers of arcs entering and leaving X, respectively.
Required entering and leaving cut capacities.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: General cut-indexed formulation allowing unequal requirements in opposite directions.

source_refs.locator: 1.2 Cut functions and connectivity concepts p. 19

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For every \(X\subseteq V\), let \(\rho_D(X)\) and \(\delta_D(X)\) denote the numbers of arcs entering and leaving \(X\). The orientation \(D\) satisfies the asymmetric directional system \((p,q)\) if
\[\rho_D(X)\ge p(X)\quad\text{and}\quad\delta_D(X)\ge q(X)\qquad(\varnothing\ne X\subsetneq V).\]
Because \(\delta_D(X)=\rho_D(V\setminus X)\), the same system can be written solely with in-cuts as
\[\rho_D(X)\ge\max\{p(X),q(V\setminus X)\}\qquad(\varnothing\ne X\subsetneq V).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each proper vertex set receives separate lower bounds on arcs entering and leaving it; complementary cuts combine these into one in-cut requirement.
knowledge_statements.title: Asymmetric Directional Requirements

source_witnesses.locator: 1.2 Cut functions and connectivity concepts p. 19

children.title: Rooted–Asymmetric Orientation Relations
children.top_down_role: Structural interaction between distinguished-root requirements and directional asymmetry.

assumptions_latex: \(D=(V,A)\) is a finite digraph with distinguished root \(r\in V\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The rooted outward and inward requirements are precisely the asymmetric cut system induced by \(p_r\) and \(q_r\).

notation.meaning: Number of arcs entering X.
Root-dependent entering and leaving requirement functions.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Encoding rooted two-directional connectivity as an asymmetric set-function system.

source_refs.locator: 9.1 Rooted k-edge-connected orientations and reorientations p. 285

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Define requirement functions on nonempty proper \(X\subset V\) by
\[p_r(X)=\begin{cases}k,&r\notin X,\\0,&r\in X,\end{cases}
\qquad
q_r(X)=\begin{cases}\ell,&r\notin X,\\0,&r\in X.\end{cases}\]
Then the asymmetric conditions \(\rho_D(X)\ge p_r(X)\) and \(\delta_D(X)\ge q_r(X)\) assert that every \(X\subseteq V\setminus\{r\}\), \(X\ne\varnothing\), has at least \(k\) entering arcs and at least \(\ell\) leaving arcs. Using \(\delta_D(X)=\rho_D(V\setminus X)\), these are exactly the two directional requirements across every root-separating cut.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rooted outward and inward connectivity are an asymmetric cut system obtained by assigning different entering and leaving demands to sets excluding the root.
knowledge_statements.title: Rooted–Asymmetric Orientation Relations

source_witnesses.locator: 9.1 Rooted k-edge-connected orientations and reorientations p. 285

children.top_down_role: Orientations coupling local degree control with connectivity requirements.

children.top_down_role: Local degree-bound orientation regimes.

children.title: Vertex In-Degree Bounds
children.top_down_role: Orientation regimes governed by local incoming-degree limits.

assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is a finite undirected multigraph without loops.
\(f,g:V\to\mathbb Z_{\ge 0}\) satisfy \(f(v)\le g(v)\) for every \(v\in V\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An orientation \(D\) respects the in-degree bounds exactly when \(f(v)\le d_D^-(v)\le g(v)\) for all \(v\in V\).

notation.meaning: In-degree of vertex v in orientation D.
Lower and upper in-degree bounds.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Vertexwise lower and upper in-degree constraints for loopless multigraph orientations.

source_refs.locator: 2.3 Degree-constrained orientations p. 58

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For an orientation \(D\) of \(G\), the in-degree \(d_D^-(v)\) is the number of edges of \(G\) oriented with head \(v\), counted with multiplicity. The orientation satisfies the vertex in-degree interval \([f,g]\) when
\[f(v)\le d_D^-(v)\le g(v)\qquad\text{for every }v\in V.\]
Because each edge has exactly one head, every such orientation also satisfies the identity \(\sum_{v\in V}d_D^-(v)=|E|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every vertex must receive a number of incoming edges lying between its prescribed lower and upper bounds.
knowledge_statements.title: Vertex In-Degree Bounds

children.title: Vertex Out-Degree Bounds
children.top_down_role: Orientation regimes governed by local outgoing-degree limits.

assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is a finite undirected multigraph without loops.
\(f,g:V\to\mathbb Z_{\ge 0}\) satisfy \(f(v)\le g(v)\) for every \(v\in V\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An orientation \(D\) respects the out-degree bounds exactly when \(f(v)\le d_D^+(v)\le g(v)\) for all \(v\in V\).

notation.meaning: Out-degree of vertex v in orientation D.
Lower and upper out-degree bounds.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Vertexwise lower and upper out-degree constraints for loopless multigraph orientations.

source_refs.locator: 2.3 Degree-constrained orientations p. 58

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For an orientation \(D\) of \(G\), the out-degree \(d_D^+(v)\) is the number of edges of \(G\) oriented with tail \(v\), counted with multiplicity. The orientation satisfies the vertex out-degree interval \([f,g]\) when
\[f(v)\le d_D^+(v)\le g(v)\qquad\text{for every }v\in V.\]
Because each edge has exactly one tail, every such orientation also satisfies the identity \(\sum_{v\in V}d_D^+(v)=|E|\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every vertex must send a number of outgoing edges lying between its prescribed lower and upper bounds.
knowledge_statements.title: Vertex Out-Degree Bounds

children.title: Joint Degree Feasibility
children.top_down_role: Compatibility regimes for simultaneous incoming-degree and outgoing-degree bounds.

assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is a finite undirected multigraph without loops.
\(a^-,b^-,a^+,b^+:V\to\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\) are prescribed lower and upper bounds.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Joint feasibility is equivalent to existence of an orientation satisfying the displayed in-degree intervals together with their induced out-degree intervals.

notation.meaning: Degree of v in the underlying undirected multigraph.
In-degree and out-degree in orientation D.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduction of paired in-out bounds to intersected in-degree intervals.

source_refs.locator: 2.3 Degree-constrained orientations p. 58

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
The four bounds are jointly feasible when an orientation \(D\) exists such that
\[a^-(v)\le d_D^-(v)\le b^-(v),\qquad a^+(v)\le d_D^+(v)\le b^+(v)\quad(v\in V).\]
Since \(d_D^-(v)+d_D^+(v)=d_G(v)\), this is equivalent to the existence of an orientation satisfying
\[\max\{a^-(v),d_G(v)-b^+(v)\}\le d_D^-(v)\le
\min\{b^-(v),d_G(v)-a^+(v)\}\quad(v\in V).\]
In particular, every resulting interval must have its lower endpoint at most its upper endpoint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Paired in-out bounds are feasible exactly when one orientation meets the in-degree intervals obtained by intersecting the direct and complementary out-degree constraints.
knowledge_statements.title: Joint Degree Feasibility

source_witnesses.locator: 2.3 Degree-constrained orientations p. 58

children.title: Connectivity Orientations with Degree Bounds
children.top_down_role: Joint global-connectivity and local-degree requirements.

assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is a finite undirected multigraph, and \(k\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A feasible orientation simultaneously satisfies every nontrivial cut lower bound and every vertex in-out degree interval.

notation.meaning: Number of arcs entering X in D.
In-degree and out-degree of v in D.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Feasibility model combining global arc-connectivity with local degree intervals.

source_refs.locator: 2.3 Degree-constrained orientations p. 58
1.2 Cut functions and connectivity concepts p. 19

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
An orientation \(D\) of \(G\) is feasible for the connectivity-and-degree instance when
\[\rho_D(X)\ge k\qquad(\varnothing\ne X\subsetneq V)\]
and, simultaneously,
\[a^-(v)\le d_D^-(v)\le b^-(v),\qquad a^+(v)\le d_D^+(v)\le b^+(v)\qquad(v\in V).\]
The cut inequalities impose global \(k\)-arc-connectivity, while the vertex inequalities impose local degree control. Feasibility means that one orientation satisfies both families; satisfying them in two different orientations is insufficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One orientation must be globally k-arc-connected while simultaneously meeting every prescribed incoming and outgoing degree interval.
knowledge_statements.title: Connectivity Orientations with Degree Bounds

source_witnesses.locator: 2.3 Degree-constrained orientations p. 58
1.2 Cut functions and connectivity concepts p. 19

children.title: Set In-Degree Requirement Orientations
children.top_down_role: Cut-indexed lower-bound orientation models.

assumptions_latex: \(h:2^V\to\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\) is a prescribed set function with \(h(\varnothing)=h(V)=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An \(h\)-covering orientation is an orientation \(D\) satisfying \(\rho_D(X)\ge h(X)\) for every \(X\subseteq V\).

notation.meaning: Number of arcs entering X in orientation D.
Required lower bound for the in-cut of X.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cut-indexed lower bounds on oriented in-degrees of vertex sets.

source_refs.locator: 1.2 Cut functions and connectivity concepts p. 19

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For an orientation \(D\) of \(G\) and a set \(X\subseteq V\), let \(\rho_D(X)\) be the number of edges directed from \(V\setminus X\) into \(X\). The orientation covers the set in-degree requirement \(h\) when
\[\rho_D(X)\ge h(X)\qquad\text{for every }X\subseteq V.\]
The endpoint conventions \(h(\varnothing)=h(V)=0\) match \(\rho_D(\varnothing)=\rho_D(V)=0\). Thus each inequality constrains the direction choices across the undirected cut determined by \(X\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each vertex set is assigned a lower bound, and enough crossing edges must be oriented into that set to meet it.
knowledge_statements.title: Set In-Degree Requirement Orientations

children.title: Generalized Orientation Domains
children.top_down_role: Connectivity orientation beyond ordinary undirected graphs.

children.title: Hypergraph Orientations
children.top_down_role: Orientation and connectivity in hypergraphic settings.

assumptions_latex: \(H=(V,\mathcal E)\) is a finite hypergraph with every \(e\in\mathcal E\) nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An orientation selects one head in each hyperedge; its in-cut counts hyperedges meeting both sides whose selected head lies inside the set.

notation.meaning: Selected head vertex of hyperedge e.
Number of oriented hyperedges entering X.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Head-selection orientation convention for finite hypergraphs.

source_refs.locator: 1.4 Special hypergraphs and bi-set systems p. 35

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A head orientation of \(H\) is a map \(h:\mathcal E\to V\) satisfying \(h(e)\in e\) for every \(e\in\mathcal E\). For \(X\subseteq V\), its entering value is
\[\rho_h(X)=\bigl|\{e\in\mathcal E:h(e)\in X\ \text{and}\ e\setminus X\ne\varnothing\}\bigr|.\]
Thus only hyperedges meeting both \(X\) and \(V\setminus X\) can enter \(X\). A cut-connectivity requirement \(r:2^V\to\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\) is covered when \(\rho_h(X)\ge r(X)\) for every \(X\subseteq V\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Orienting a hyperedge selects its head vertex; a hyperedge enters a set when its head is inside and another incident vertex is outside.
knowledge_statements.title: Hypergraph Orientations

children.title: Mixed-Graph Partial-Orientation Completion Interface
children.top_down_role: Completion and modification of partially directed graphs.

children.title: Mixed-Graph Orientation Extensions
children.top_down_role: Connectivity orientation problems on graphs containing edges and fixed arcs.

assumptions_latex: \(M=(V,A\cup E)\) is a finite mixed graph, with fixed arcs \(A\) and undirected edges \(E\).
\(f:2^V\to\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\) is a prescribed in-cut requirement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An orientation extension is feasible exactly when its total in-cut, including fixed arcs, covers \(f(X)\) for every \(X\subseteq V\).

notation.meaning: Number of fixed arcs entering X.
Number of newly oriented edges entering X.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Extension of cut-covering orientation models to mixed graphs with immutable arcs.

source_refs.locator: 9.5 Mixed graphs and orientations p. 312

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Choose an orientation \(D_E\) of every edge in \(E\), while leaving every arc in \(A\) unchanged. The resulting directed extension satisfies the set requirement \(f\) when
\[\rho_A(X)+\rho_{D_E}(X)\ge f(X)\qquad\text{for every }X\subseteq V.\]
Equivalently, the undirected edges must cover the residual requirement
\[f_A(X)=\max\{0,f(X)-\rho_A(X)\},\]
so that \(\rho_{D_E}(X)\ge f_A(X)\) for every \(X\subseteq V\). Fixed arcs contribute connectivity but cannot be reversed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixed arcs remain unchanged, while undirected edges are oriented to cover whatever part of each in-cut requirement the fixed arcs do not supply.
knowledge_statements.title: Mixed-Graph Orientation Extensions

source_witnesses.locator: 9.5 Mixed graphs and orientations p. 312

children.title: Partial-Orientation Completion

assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is a finite undirected graph and \(E=E_0\mathbin{\dot\cup}E_1\).

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A completion of \(D_0\) is an orientation \(D_1\) of \(E_1\); the union \(D=D_0\cup D_1\) preserves every prescribed direction. It is an \(f\)-covering completion when
\[\rho_{D_0}(X)+\rho_{D_1}(X)\ge f(X)\qquad(X\subseteq V).\]
Define the residual demand by \(f_0(X)=\max\{0,f(X)-\rho_{D_0}(X)\}\). Then an \(f\)-covering completion exists if and only if \(E_1\) has an orientation \(D_1\) satisfying \(\rho_{D_1}(X)\ge f_0(X)\) for every \(X\subseteq V\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Complete a partial orientation by directing every remaining edge so that the new arcs cover all cut demand not already met by prescribed arcs.

children.title: Fixed-Arc Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Structural compatibility between immutable arcs and target connectivity.

knowledge_statements.title: Fixed-Arc Compatibility
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cut criterion for completing a partially oriented multigraph to a strong orientation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M=(V,A\cup E)\) be a finite mixed multigraph, where arcs in \(A\) are fixed and edges in \(E\) remain unoriented. For \(X\subset V\), let \(\delta_E(X)\) be the unoriented edges crossing \((X,V\setminus X)\), and let \(\rho_A(X)\) be the fixed arcs entering \(X\). The fixed arcs are compatible with a strong completion precisely when
\[|\rho_A(X)|+|\delta_E(X)|\ge 1\qquad(\varnothing\ne X\subsetneq V).\]
Equivalently, no nontrivial cut is devoid of an edge that can be directed into its chosen side. Under this condition the edges in \(E\) can be oriented while every arc in \(A\) retains its prescribed direction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A partial orientation has a strongly connected completion exactly when every nontrivial vertex set has either a fixed entering arc or an unoriented crossing edge.
assumptions_latex: \(M\) is finite; parallel edges are allowed and loops are irrelevant.
Only edges in \(E\) may be oriented.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M\) admits a strong orientation extending \(A\) if and only if \(|\rho_A(X)|+|\delta_E(X)|\ge1\) for every \(\varnothing\ne X\subsetneq V\).

notation.meaning: Fixed arcs entering X
