children.title: Minimum-Cost Connectivity Orientations
children.top_down_role: Costed selection of directions subject to connectivity requirements.

knowledge_statements.title: Minimum-Cost Connectivity Orientations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimum-cost strong orientation with direction-dependent edge costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a finite undirected multigraph. For each edge \(e=uv\), assign finite directional costs \(c_e(u,v)\) and \(c_e(v,u)\). A minimum-cost connectivity orientation is an orientation \(D\) of every edge minimizing
\[c(D)=\sum_{e=uv\in E}c_e(D(e))\]
subject to \(D\) being strongly connected, equivalently \(|\rho_D(X)|\ge1\) for every \(\varnothing\ne X\subsetneq V\). If no feasible orientation exists, the optimum value is \(+\infty\). More generally, replacing the right-hand side by \(k\) defines the minimum-cost \(k\)-arc-connected orientation problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose one direction for every edge at minimum total directional cost while ensuring at least one arc enters every nontrivial vertex set.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is finite, and directional costs are additive.
Strong connectivity is the required connectivity notion.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{OPT}=\min\{c(D):D\text{ orients }G,\ |\rho_D(X)|\ge1\text{ for all }\varnothing\ne X\subsetneq V\}\).

notation.meaning: Direction assigned to edge e

children.title: Strongly Connected Reorientation
children.top_down_role: Modification of an existing orientation to obtain strong connectivity.

knowledge_statements.title: Strongly Connected Reorientation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimum-cost reversal of an existing orientation into a strongly connected digraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D_0=(V,A)\) be a finite digraph whose underlying undirected multigraph is \(G\), and assign each arc \(a\in A\) a nonnegative reversal cost \(w_a\). For \(R\subseteq A\), let \(D_0^R\) be obtained by reversing precisely the arcs in \(R\). The strongly connected reorientation problem is
\[\min\left\{\sum_{a\in R}w_a:R\subseteq A,\ D_0^R\text{ is strongly connected}\right\}.\]
Feasibility depends only on \(G\): a feasible reorientation exists exactly when \(G\) is connected and has no bridge. The unweighted version takes \(w_a=1\) and minimizes the number of reversed arcs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Reverse a minimum-cost subset of existing arcs so that the resulting digraph is strongly connected; feasibility requires a bridgeless connected underlying graph.
assumptions_latex: \(D_0\) is finite, and every arc may be reversed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{OPT}=\min_{R\subseteq A}\{w(R):D_0^R\text{ is strong}\}\), with finite optimum exactly when the underlying graph is bridgeless and connected.

notation.meaning: Digraph obtained by reversing arcs in R

children.title: Well-Balanced Orientations
children.top_down_role: Orientation families balancing directed local connectivities.

knowledge_statements.title: Well-Balanced Orientations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pairwise edge-connectivity form of the well-balanced orientation theorem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For a finite undirected multigraph \(G=(V,E)\), let \(\lambda_G(u,v)\) denote the minimum size of an undirected cut separating distinct vertices \(u,v\). For an orientation \(D\) of \(G\), let \(\lambda_D(u,v)\) be the maximum number of pairwise arc-disjoint directed \(u\)-to-\(v\) paths. There exists an orientation \(D\) such that, for every ordered pair of distinct vertices,
\[\lambda_D(u,v)\ge \left\lfloor\frac{\lambda_G(u,v)}2\right\rfloor.\]
Such an orientation is called well-balanced. Consequently, both directed local connectivities between each unordered pair attain at least half the undirected local connectivity, rounded down.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Every finite undirected multigraph can be oriented so each directed local connectivity is at least half the corresponding undirected connectivity, rounded down.
assumptions_latex: Local connectivity is measured by edge- or arc-disjoint paths.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There is an orientation \(D\) satisfying \(\lambda_D(u,v)\ge\lfloor\lambda_G(u,v)/2\rfloor\) for all distinct \(u,v\in V\).

notation.meaning: Undirected local edge connectivity

children.title: Bridge Obstructions
children.top_down_role: Bridge structures preventing strongly connected orientations.

knowledge_statements.title: Bridge Obstructions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Sharp bridge obstruction to strongly orienting an undirected multigraph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a finite connected undirected multigraph. If \(e\) is a bridge, then every orientation of \(e\) leaves one side of \(G-e\) with no directed arc entering it or no directed arc leaving it; hence no orientation of \(G\) is strongly connected. Conversely, if \(G\) has no bridge, then \(G\) admits a strongly connected orientation. Thus
\[G\text{ is strongly orientable}\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad G\text{ is 2-edge-connected},\]
where 2-edge-connected means connected and bridgeless.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A connected undirected multigraph has a strongly connected orientation exactly when it has no bridge.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is a finite connected undirected multigraph.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G\) admits a strong orientation if and only if every nontrivial cut has at least two edges.

children.title: Sparse-Cut Obstructions

knowledge_statements.title: Sparse-Cut Obstructions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cut-size obstruction and sharp threshold for globally arc-connected orientations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Fix an integer \(k\ge1\) and let \(G=(V,E)\) be a finite undirected multigraph. If an orientation \(D\) is \(k\)-arc-connected, then every nonempty proper \(X\subset V\) has at least \(k\) arcs entering and \(k\) arcs leaving. Therefore
\[|\delta_G(X)|\ge2k\qquad(\varnothing\ne X\subsetneq V).\]
Any cut with fewer than \(2k\) edges is consequently an obstruction. Conversely, if every nontrivial cut of \(G\) has at least \(2k\) edges, then \(G\) admits a \(k\)-arc-connected orientation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An undirected graph admits a k-arc-connected orientation exactly when every nontrivial cut contains at least 2k edges.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G\) has a \(k\)-arc-connected orientation if and only if \(|\delta_G(X)|\ge2k\) for every \(\varnothing\ne X\subsetneq V\).

notation.meaning: Edges with exactly one endpoint in X

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition of a numerical severity measure for failure of the cut condition for k-arc-connected orientability.

source_refs.locator: 1.2 Cut functions and connectivity concepts p. 19

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a finite undirected multigraph with \(|V|\ge 2\), and let \(k\ge 1\) be an integer. For every \(\varnothing\ne X\subsetneq V\), define the cut deficit by
\[\operatorname{def}_k(X)=\max\{0,2k-|\delta_G(X)|\},\]
and define the cut-deficit severity by
\[\Delta_k(G)=\max_{\varnothing\ne X\subsetneq V}\operatorname{def}_k(X).\]
A set \(X\) attaining a positive maximum is a verifiable certificate that no \(k\)-arc-connected orientation exists. Moreover, \(\Delta_k(G)=0\) exactly when every nontrivial cut has size at least \(2k\), equivalently when \(G\) admits a \(k\)-arc-connected orientation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Cut-deficit severity is the largest shortfall of a nontrivial cut from size 2k. A positive maximizing cut certifies that a k-arc-connected orientation is impossible, while zero severity characterizes orientability.
knowledge_statements.title: Cut-Deficit Severity

knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a finite undirected multigraph, let \(D\) be a \(k\)-arc-connected orientation of \(G\), where \(k\ge 1\), and let \(b^+,b^-:V\to\mathbb Z_{\ge 0}\) be prescribed outdegree and indegree upper bounds. Applying the directed cut requirements to \(\{v\}\) gives
\[d_D^+(v)\ge k,\qquad d_D^-(v)\ge k\qquad(v\in V),\]
and hence \(d_G(v)\ge 2k\). Therefore the bounds \(d_D^+(v)\le b^+(v)\) and \(d_D^-(v)\le b^-(v)\) conflict with \(k\)-arc-connectivity whenever \(b^+(v)<k\), \(b^-(v)<k\), or \(d_G(v)<2k\) for some \(v\in V\). These local inequalities are necessary but not generally sufficient for a degree-constrained connectivity orientation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A k-arc-connected orientation needs at least k incoming and k outgoing arcs at every vertex, so an upper bound below k or an undirected degree below 2k immediately obstructs feasibility.

children.title: Partial-Orientation Extension Obstructions
children.top_down_role: Obstructions arising from fixed arcs in mixed or partially oriented graphs.

knowledge_statements.title: Partial-Orientation Extension Obstructions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cut certificates preventing extension of fixed arcs to k-arc-connectivity.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(M=(V,A\cup E)\) be a finite mixed multigraph, with fixed arcs \(A\) and unoriented edges \(E\), and let \(k\ge1\). For every nonempty proper \(X\subset V\), any completion \(D\) satisfies
\[|\rho_D(X)|\le |\rho_A(X)|+|\delta_E(X)|.\]
Consequently, if
\[|\rho_A(X)|+|\delta_E(X)|<k\]
for some \(X\), then no orientation of \(E\) extending the fixed arcs can be \(k\)-arc-connected. Such a set \(X\), together with its fixed entering arcs and crossing unoriented edges, is a directly checkable extension-obstruction certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A fixed partial orientation cannot extend to k-arc-connectivity if some set has fewer than k possible entering arcs, even after orienting every crossing free edge inward.
assumptions_latex: \(M\) is finite, and arcs in \(A\) cannot be reversed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If \(|\rho_A(X)|+|\delta_E(X)|<k\) for some nontrivial \(X\), no \(k\)-arc-connected completion exists.

notation.meaning: Fixed arcs entering X

knowledge_statements.title: Orientation Tractability Boundaries
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algorithmic boundary for unconstrained strong orientability of undirected multigraphs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a finite undirected multigraph \(G=(V,E)\) in adjacency-list representation, feasibility of a strongly connected orientation can be decided in \(O(|V|+|E|)\) time by computing connected components and bridges. If \(G\) is connected and bridgeless, a depth-first-search ear-orientation construction produces a strong orientation within the same asymptotic time; otherwise a component separation or bridge is an infeasibility certificate. This bound concerns unconstrained strong orientation only and does not classify variants with fixed arcs, degree restrictions, multiple connectivity levels, or additional side constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Unconstrained strong orientability is decidable and constructible in linear time by testing connectivity and bridges; constrained variants fall outside this bound.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is a finite undirected multigraph stored by adjacency lists.
The task has no costs, fixed directions, or degree side constraints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Strong-orientation feasibility and construction require \(O(|V|+|E|)\) time in the adjacency-list model.

children.title: Reorientation Hardness Regimes

knowledge_statements.title: Reorientation Hardness Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Decision template separating reorientation variants by permitted reversals and side constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A constrained reorientation decision instance consists of a digraph \(D_0=(V,A)\), a reversible set \(F\subseteq A\), reversal costs \(w:F\to\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}\), a budget \(B\), and a specified connectivity predicate \(\mathcal C\). Its question is whether there exists \(R\subseteq F\) such that
\[\sum_{a\in R}w(a)\le B\quad\text{and}\quad D_0^R\in\mathcal C.\]
A hardness regime is determined by the choices of \(\mathcal C\), restrictions on \(F\), and any degree or local-connectivity side constraints. The template itself makes no uniform hardness claim: distinct specializations can have different computational complexity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reorientation hardness regime fixes which arcs may reverse, a budget, a target connectivity property, and any side constraints; complexity depends on that specialization.
assumptions_latex: Costs and the budget are encoded as part of the instance.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The associated decision predicate is \(\exists R\subseteq F:\ w(R)\le B\text{ and }D_0^R\in\mathcal C\).

notation.meaning: Set of arcs eligible for reversal
Digraph after reversing precisely R
Required connectivity class

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Minimum-Weight Connectivity Augmentation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines weighted connectivity augmentation and records the source's hardness and approximation boundaries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given $G=(V,E)$ with nonnegative edge weights, a spanning subgraph $G_0=(V,E_0)$, and a prescribed connectivity level $\lambda$, find a minimum-weight set $\mathrm{Aug}\subseteq E\setminus E_0$ such that $(V,E_0\cup\mathrm{Aug})$ is $\lambda$-connected under the edge- or vertex-connectivity variant being considered. Only edges of $G$ may be added. The source states that the problem is NP-hard for $\lambda>1$ and that a polynomial-time factor-$2$ approximation is available for every $\lambda$ for both variants. For $\lambda=2$ and connected $G_0$, a factor-$2$ algorithm is stated; if $G_0$ is disconnected, its components may first be connected by a minimum spanning tree.

The source states NP-hardness above connectivity one and polynomial-time factor-2 approximations for every prescribed level.

children.title: Deficient Cut Families

knowledge_statements.title: Deficient Cut Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cut-indexed residual requirements for an edge-connectivity augmentation instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(H=(V,E_H)\) be a finite undirected multigraph and let \(r:2^V\to\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\) specify required cut connectivities, with \(r(\varnothing)=r(V)=0\). For \(X\subseteq V\), define the residual cut deficiency
\[p_H(X)=\max\{0,r(X)-|\delta_H(X)|\}.\]
The deficient cut family is
\[\mathcal F_H=\{X:\varnothing\ne X\subsetneq V,\ p_H(X)>0\}.\]
If an augmenting edge set \(J\) makes every cut meet its requirement, then it must cover each deficiency: \(|\delta_J(X)|\ge p_H(X)\) for every \(X\in\mathcal F_H\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Deficient cuts are vertex sets whose current cut size is below its requirement; any augmentation must add enough crossing edges to cover every residual deficit.
assumptions_latex: \(r(X)\) is an integer cut requirement with \(r(\varnothing)=r(V)=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every feasible augmentation \(J\) satisfies \(|\delta_J(X)|\ge p_H(X)\) for all \(X\in\mathcal F_H\).

A biset is a pair \(\hat X=(X,X^{+})\) with \(X\subseteq X^{+}\subseteq V\). Its boundary is \(\Gamma(\hat X)=X^{+}\setminus X\), and its outer complement is \(X^{*}=V\setminus X^{+}\). For an edge set \(H\), let \(d_H(A,B)\) denote the number of edges of \(H\) joining disjoint sets \(A\) and \(B\). For \(X\ne\varnothing\) and \(X^{*}\ne\varnothing\), define \[p_G(\hat X)=\max\{0,\,k-|\Gamma(\hat X)|-d_E(X,X^{*})\}.\] The set \(J\) covers \(\hat X\) when \(d_J(X,X^{*})\ge p_G(\hat X)\), and the biset deficiency model imposes this inequality for every such biset.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A biset records an inner side, its boundary, and an outer complement. Its deficiency is the target vertex-connectivity minus the boundary size and the number of existing edges between the separated sides; selected candidate edges must cover the positive shortfall.
knowledge_statements.title: Biset Deficiency Models

children.title: Representation Equivalence Regimes
children.top_down_role: Settings where set-pair and biset deficiency views correspond.

knowledge_statements.title: Representation Equivalence Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact equivalence between ordered set pairs and proper bisets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For every ordered set pair \((U,W)\) of nonempty disjoint subsets of \(V\), define \(\hat X=(U,V\setminus W)\). Conversely, for every biset \(\hat X=(X,X^{+})\) with nonempty inner set and outer complement, define \((U,W)=(X,V\setminus X^{+})\). These maps are inverse, and \[\Gamma(\hat X)=V\setminus(U\cup W),\qquad X^{*}=W.\] Consequently, \[p_G(U,W)=p_G(\hat X),\qquad d_J(U,W)=d_J(X,X^{*}).\] Hence the set-pair and biset covering systems have identical feasible augmentations whenever their deficiencies use these corresponding formulas.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Proper bisets and ordered disjoint set pairs are bijective. Under the mapping, their boundaries, deficiencies, covering edges, and feasible augmentations coincide.
assumptions_latex: The set-pair and biset deficiencies use the same graph \(G\) and target \(k\).
Only set pairs with two nonempty sides and bisets with nonempty inner and outer-complement sides are included.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The two representations define the same covering inequalities after the substitution \(\hat X=(U,V\setminus W)\).

notation.meaning: Biset corresponding to the ordered set pair.
Outer complement, corresponding to W.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The stated bijection and incidence identities are mathematically plausible, but no source with an inspectable locator is supplied. The record is a representation equivalence, not a mathematical duality, so content_kind should be representation once sourced.

children.title: Laminar Deficiency Core Hierarchy

children.title: Deficiency Uncrossing
children.top_down_role: Uncrossing structure within families of deficient cuts or bisets.

knowledge_statements.title: Deficiency Uncrossing
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Uncrossing rule for skew-supermodular deficiency functions on cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p:2^{V}\to\mathbb R_{+}\) be skew-supermodular: for every \(X,Y\subseteq V\), at least one inequality \[p(X)+p(Y)\le p(X\cap Y)+p(X\cup Y)\] or \[p(X)+p(Y)\le p(X\setminus Y)+p(Y\setminus X)\] holds. Let \(x\ge0\) satisfy \(x(\delta(Z))\ge p(Z)\) for all \(Z\subseteq V\). If crossing sets \(X,Y\) are tight and one displayed inequality is the applicable skew-supermodular inequality, submodularity or posimodularity of the cut function implies that the corresponding uncrossed sets are also tight.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two crossing tight deficient cuts can be replaced by their intersection and union, or by their differences, whenever the matching skew-supermodular inequality applies.
assumptions_latex: \(V\) is finite and \(p\) is nonnegative and skew-supermodular.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The applicable uncrossed pair is tight and may replace \(X,Y\) without losing the tightness certificate.

notation.meaning: Edges with exactly one endpoint in X.
Total x-value on the cut of X.
Cut-deficiency requirement function.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conditional uncrossing statement is standard and coherent, but the theorem-level assertion that the appropriate uncrossed pair is tight requires a source with a specific theorem, section, or page locator.

children.title: Minimal Deficiency Cores
children.top_down_role: Minimal deficient members serving as compact structural witnesses.

knowledge_statements.title: Minimal Deficiency Cores
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Inclusion-minimal positive members of a deficiency system.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p:2^{V}\to\mathbb R_{+}\) be a deficiency function. A set \(C\subseteq V\) is a minimal deficiency core if \[p(C)>0\quad\text{and}\quad p(Z)=0\ \text{for every proper subset }Z\subsetneq C.\] Relative to a current augmentation vector \(x\), a residual core is defined analogously using \(p_x(Z)=\max\{0,p(Z)-x(\delta(Z))\}\). Thus a residual core is an inclusion-minimal set whose covering inequality remains violated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A deficiency core is an inclusion-minimal set with positive deficiency; residually, it is a minimal set whose covering inequality is still violated.
assumptions_latex: \(p:2^{V}\to\mathbb R_{+}\) is a specified deficiency function.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(C\) is a core exactly when it has positive deficiency and every proper subset has zero deficiency.

notation.meaning: A minimal deficiency core.
Deficiency remaining after augmentation vector x.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The static core definition is precise, but the residual version does not specify the edge universe or the domain and nonnegativity of x. No source locator is supplied for either the core terminology or its residual variant.

children.title: Laminar Deficiency Families
children.top_down_role: Nested deficiency structures arising from uncrossing and core selection.

knowledge_statements.title: Laminar Deficiency Families
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Laminar optimal support obtained by uncrossing a cut-covering dual.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(p:2^{V}\to\mathbb Z_{+}\) be skew-supermodular and let \(c\in\mathbb R_{+}^{E}\). Consider the dual cut-packing system \[\max\left\{\sum_{X\subseteq V}p(X)y_X:\ \sum_{X:e\in\delta(X)}y_X\le c_e\ \text{for all }e\in E,\ y\ge0\right\}.\] If this finite linear program has an optimum, then it has an optimal solution \(y\) whose positive support is laminar: for any supported \(X,Y\), either \(X\subseteq Y\), \(Y\subseteq X\), or \(X\cap Y=\varnothing\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: For a skew-supermodular cut requirement, an optimal dual packing can be chosen with laminar positive support.
assumptions_latex: The displayed dual has an optimal solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exists an optimal dual solution whose support \(\{X:y_X>0\}\) is laminar.

notation.meaning: Dual weight assigned to cut X.
Capacity of edge e in the dual packing.
Cut induced by X.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This is a substantive laminar-support theorem rather than a definition. Its hypotheses and conclusion are plausible, and theorem is the correct content kind, but no authoritative locator is provided for the skew-supermodular dual uncrossing result.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a finite undirected graph, let \(F\) be a finite set of candidate undirected edges on \(V\), let \(c_e\ge0\) be the cost of each \(e\in F\), and let \(p(X)\in\mathbb Z_{+}\) be the residual requirement of every nonempty proper set \(X\subset V\). With variables \(z_e\in\{0,1\}\) for \(e\in F\), the minimum-cost cut-covering model is \[\min\left\{\sum_{e\in F}c_ez_e:\ \sum_{e\in F\cap\delta(X)}z_e\ge p(X)\text{ for every }\varnothing\ne X\subsetneq V,\ z_e\in\{0,1\}\text{ for every }e\in F\right\}.\] Its linear relaxation replaces \(z_e\in\{0,1\}\) by \(0\le z_e\le1\) for every \(e\in F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose minimum-cost candidate edges so that every nonempty proper cut receives at least its prescribed residual number of crossing edges; the linear relaxation permits fractional selection between zero and one.

children.title: Connector Models
children.top_down_role: Augmentation models organized around connector structures spanning connectivity deficits.

knowledge_statements.title: Connector Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Connector sets for a family of deficient separations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be a set of candidate edges and let \(\mathcal D\) be a family of deficient set pairs with integer demands \(p(U,W)>0\). An edge \(e=uv\in F\) connects \((U,W)\) if one endpoint lies in \(U\) and the other in \(W\). A set \(J\subseteq F\) is a connector for \((\mathcal D,p)\) if \[d_J(U,W)\ge p(U,W)\qquad\text{for every }(U,W)\in\mathcal D.\] For unit demands, every deficient pair must be connected by at least one selected edge.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A connector is a candidate-edge set containing enough direct edges between the two sides of every deficient set pair.
assumptions_latex: Each demand \(p(U,W)\) is a positive integer.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(J\) is a connector exactly when it supplies at least \(p(U,W)\) connecting edges to every member of \(\mathcal D\).

notation.meaning: Family of deficient set pairs.
Number of selected edges directly joining U and W.
Required connector multiplicity for the pair.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The connector definition is plausible and definition is the appropriate content kind, but the vertex ground set and admissibility conditions on each set pair are not stated. No source with a specific locator supports the terminology or model.

children.title: Cover–Connector Correspondence
children.top_down_role: Structural translations between cut-covering and connector viewpoints.

knowledge_statements.title: Cover–Connector Correspondence
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Incidence-preserving equivalence of cut covers and connectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Associate with each deficient set pair \((U,W)\) the cut-like object whose covering candidates are \(\delta_F(U,W)=\{uv\in F:u\in U,v\in W\text{ or }u\in W,v\in U\}\). For every \(J\subseteq F\), \[|J\cap\delta_F(U,W)|=d_J(U,W).\] Therefore the covering inequality \(|J\cap\delta_F(U,W)|\ge p(U,W)\) is identical to the connector inequality \(d_J(U,W)\ge p(U,W)\). Applying this identity to every deficient pair gives a bijection between feasible cut covers and feasible connectors, preserving selected edges and total edge cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A candidate edge covers a deficient pair exactly when it connects its two sides, so feasible covers and connectors are the same edge sets with the same costs.
assumptions_latex: Cut-cover and connector models use the same candidate set \(F\).
Both models assign the same demand \(p(U,W)\) to each deficient pair.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The identity map on subsets of \(F\) is a cost-preserving bijection between feasible covers and feasible connectors.

notation.meaning: Candidate edges joining the two sides of a set pair.
Selected augmentation-edge set.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The incidence identity is mathematically immediate, but the claimed model correspondence has no cited source. It is an equivalence of representations, not a duality, so representation is the appropriate content kind once the claim is sourced.

children.title: Undirected Edge-Connectivity Augmentation
children.top_down_role: Cardinality and connector regimes for augmenting undirected edge connectivity.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Disjoint-Set Characterization of Bounded-Size k-Edge-Connectors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary and sufficient feasibility characterization for undirected edge-connectivity augmentation with a cardinality budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be an undirected graph and let \(k,\gamma\in\mathbb Z_+\) with \(k\ge2\). The graph \(G\) has a \(k\)-edge-connector of cardinality at most \(\gamma\) if and only if, for every collection \(\mathcal P\) of pairwise disjoint nonempty proper subsets of \(V\), \[2\gamma\ge\sum_{U\in\mathcal P}\bigl(k-d_E(U)\bigr).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An undirected graph admits a k-edge-connector using at most gamma edges exactly when the total connectivity deficit of every collection of pairwise disjoint nonempty proper vertex sets is at most twice gamma.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists F\;\bigl[F\text{ is a }k\text{-edge-connector and }|F|\le\gamma\bigr]\iff\forall\mathcal P\subseteq 2^V\;\left[\begin{array}{l}\mathcal P\text{ consists of pairwise disjoint nonempty proper subsets of }V\\{}\Longrightarrow 2\gamma\ge\sum_{U\in\mathcal P}(k-d_E(U))\end{array}\right].

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Min-max formula for minimum-cardinality r-edge-connectors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Gives a marginal-component reduction and a disjoint-set min-max characterization when no marginal component remains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be an undirected graph and let \(r:V\times V\to\mathbb Z_+\) satisfy \(r(u,v)=r(v,u)\ge\lambda_G(u,v)\) for all \(u,v\in V\) and \(r(u,w)\ge\min\{r(u,v),r(v,w)\}\) for all \(u,v,w\in V\). Let \(R\) and marginal components be defined as above. If \(K\) is a marginal component, then \[\gamma(G,r)=\gamma(G-K,r')+R(K),\] where \(r'\) is the restriction of \(r\) to \((V\setminus K)\times(V\setminus K)\). If \(G\) has no marginal components, then \[\gamma(G,r)=\max_{\mathcal P}\left\lceil\frac12\sum_{U\in\mathcal P}\left(R(U)-d_E(U)\right)\right\rceil,\] where \(\mathcal P\) ranges over all collections of pairwise disjoint nonempty proper subsets of \(V\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A marginal component contributes exactly R(K) to the minimum connector size and can be removed recursively. If no marginal component exists, the minimum number of added edges is the maximum rounded half-sum of cut deficits over collections of pairwise disjoint nonempty proper vertex subsets.
assumptions_latex: R\text{ and marginal components are defined by (63.59) and the preceding definition}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: K\text{ marginal}\Rightarrow\gamma(G,r)=\gamma(G-K,r')+R(K);\qquad G\text{ has no marginal components}\Rightarrow\gamma(G,r)=\max_{\mathcal P}\left\lceil\frac12\sum_{U\in\mathcal P}(R(U)-d_E(U))\right\rceil

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Undirected k-Edge-Connector
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines augmentation by an undirected edge set, including the convention for edges common to the original and augmenting graphs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) and \((V,F)\) be undirected graphs. The set \(F\) is a \(k\)-edge-connector for \(G\) if \((V,E\cup F)\) is \(k\)-edge-connected, where an edge occurring in both \(E\) and \(F\) is retained as two parallel edges in \(E\cup F\).

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: F\text{ is a }k\text{-edge-connector for }G\iff (V,E\cup F)\text{ is }k\text{-edge-connected}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: r-edge-connectivity and r-edge-connectors
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines pairwise-demand edge connectivity and augmentation, gives the cut representation, and records the stated costed-versus-cardinality complexity boundary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an undirected graph \(G=(V,E)\) and \(r:V\times V\to\mathbb Z_+\), \(G\) is \(r\)-edge-connected if every \(u,v\in V\) are joined by at least \(r(u,v)\) edge-disjoint paths. Equivalently, \(d_E(U)\ge r(u,v)\) for every \(U\subseteq V\), \(u\in U\), and \(v\in V\setminus U\). An \(r\)-edge-connector is an edge set \(F\) on \(V\), with parallel edges allowed, such that \(\lambda_{(V,E\uplus F)}(u,v)\ge r(u,v)\) for all \(u,v\in V\), and \(\gamma(G,r)\) is the minimum cardinality of such an \(F\). The minimum-cost version with \(k:V\times V\to\mathbb Q_+\) is NP-complete as stated in the source, already for \(E=\varnothing\) and \(r\equiv2\), whereas the cardinality case has a polynomial-time algorithm and a min-max formula.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pairwise edge-connectivity demands have equivalent path and cut descriptions. An r-edge-connector adds edges, allowing parallel copies, until every pair meets its demand, and gamma(G,r) is its minimum size. The source states that the costed problem is NP-complete even for an empty graph and uniform demand two, while the cardinality problem is polynomially solvable and has a min-max formula.
assumptions_latex: k:V\times V\to\mathbb Q_+\text{ in the costed variant}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: G\text{ is }r\text{-edge-connected}\iff d_E(U)\ge r(u,v)\ \forall U\subseteq V,\ u\in U,\ v\notin U;\quad \gamma(G,r)=\min\{|F|:F\text{ is an }r\text{-edge-connector}\}

knowledge_statements.title: Two-Edge-Connectivity Augmentation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cut formulation of bridge elimination in an undirected graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a connected undirected graph and let \(F\) be candidate edges. Define \[p_2(X)=\max\{0,\,2-d_E(X,V\setminus X)\}\qquad(\varnothing\ne X\subsetneq V).\] An augmentation \(J\subseteq F\) makes \(G+J\) two-edge-connected if and only if \[d_J(X,V\setminus X)\ge p_2(X)\qquad\text{for every nonempty proper }X\subset V.\] Equivalently, every bridge cut of \(G\) is crossed by a selected candidate edge; cuts already containing at least two original edges impose no residual demand.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Two-edge-connectivity augmentation selects edges crossing every bridge cut; equivalently, each proper cut must contain at least two original or added edges.
assumptions_latex: \(F\) consists of additional undirected edges on \(V\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G+J\) is two-edge-connected exactly when \(d_E(X,V\setminus X)+d_J(X,V\setminus X)\ge2\) for every proper nonempty \(X\).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact cardinality formula for possibly disconnected forests in terms of leaves and isolated vertices.

knowledge_statements.title: Higher Edge-Connectivity Augmentation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Global cut formulation for undirected target edge-connectivity \(k\ge3\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be an undirected graph, let \(F\) be candidate edges, and fix \(k\ge3\). For every nonempty proper \(X\subset V\), define \[p_k(X)=\max\{0,\,k-d_E(X,V\setminus X)\}.\] An augmentation \(J\subseteq F\) makes \(G+J\) globally \(k\)-edge-connected if and only if \[d_J(X,V\setminus X)\ge p_k(X)\qquad\text{for every nonempty proper }X\subset V.\] Thus higher edge-connectivity augmentation is precisely the covering of all residual cut deficiencies.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: To reach global edge-connectivity k, added edges must cover every proper cut's shortfall below k.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) and \(F\) are finite undirected graphs on the same vertex set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(G+J\) is \(k\)-edge-connected exactly when every nontrivial cut has at least \(k\) original or added edges.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Iterative residual-forest construction for lambda edge connectivity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Construction that begins with a DFS-derived 2-edge-connected subgraph and successively adds spanning forests from residual graphs; the extract states no correctness, feasibility, or approximation guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Find a 2-edge-connected subgraph \(H_2\) using the DFS-based algorithm. For \(i=3,\ldots,\lambda\), let \(T_i\) be a spanning forest in \(G-H_{i-1}\) and define \(H_i=H_{i-1}\cup T_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: First find a 2-edge-connected subgraph using the DFS-based algorithm. For each index from 3 through lambda, find a spanning forest in the graph remaining outside the current subgraph and add that forest to form the next subgraph.

knowledge_statements.title: Rooted Edge-Connectivity Augmentation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cut characterization of augmentation from a designated root.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be an undirected graph with root \(r\in V\), let \(F\) be candidate edges, and fix \(k\ge1\). For every nonempty \(X\subseteq V\setminus\{r\}\), define \[p_r(X)=\max\{0,\,k-d_E(X,V\setminus X)\}.\] An augmentation \(J\subseteq F\) provides \(k\) edge-disjoint paths from \(r\) to every vertex \(v\ne r\) if and only if \[d_J(X,V\setminus X)\ge p_r(X)\qquad\text{for every nonempty }X\subseteq V\setminus\{r\}.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Rooted k-edge-connectivity is obtained exactly when added edges cover every cut separating the root from at least one other vertex up to capacity k.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) and \(F\) are finite undirected graphs on \(V\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: For every \(v\ne r\), the graph \(G+J\) contains \(k\) edge-disjoint \(r\)-to-\(v\) paths exactly when all rooted cut inequalities hold.

knowledge_statements.title: Strong Arc-Connectivity Augmentation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Minimum-cost augmentation to global directed arc-connectivity at least \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\) be a finite digraph, let \(F\subseteq V\times V\) be candidate arcs with costs \(c:F\to\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}\), and let \(k\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 1}\). Strong arc-connectivity augmentation seeks \(J\subseteq F\) minimizing \(c(J)=\sum_{e\in J}c(e)\) such that \(D+J=(V,A\cup J)\) is \(k\)-arc-strong. Equivalently, every nonempty proper set \(X\subset V\) satisfies \[|\delta^-_{D+J}(X)|\ge k\quad\text{and}\quad |\delta^+_{D+J}(X)|\ge k.\] Parallel candidate arcs may be represented as distinct elements of \(F\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Choose minimum-cost candidate arcs so every nontrivial vertex set has at least k entering and k leaving arcs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Find \(J\subseteq F\) of minimum cost with \(D+J\) \(k\)-arc-strong.

notation.meaning: Arcs entering and leaving X in D.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Min-max criterion for a bounded-size k-arc-connector
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes global directed arc-connectivity augmentation under a cardinality budget.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let $D=(V,A)$ be a directed graph and $k,\gamma\in\mathbb Z_+$. A $k$-arc-connector of size at most $\gamma$ exists if and only if, for every collection $\mathcal P$ of pairwise disjoint nonempty proper subsets of $V$, $$\gamma\ge\sum_{X\in\mathcal P}\bigl(k-d_A^{\mathrm{in}}(X)\bigr),\qquad \gamma\ge\sum_{X\in\mathcal P}\bigl(k-d_A^{\mathrm{out}}(X)\bigr).$$
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A directed graph can be made k-arc-connected by adding at most gamma arcs exactly when gamma is at least both the total entering-cut deficit and the total leaving-cut deficit for every collection of pairwise disjoint nonempty proper vertex subsets.
assumptions_latex: \mathcal P\text{ ranges over collections of pairwise disjoint nonempty proper subsets of }V
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists B\;\bigl[B\text{ is a }k\text{-arc-connector and }|B|\le\gamma\bigr]\iff\forall\mathcal P:\ \gamma\ge\sum_{X\in\mathcal P}(k-d_A^{\mathrm{in}}(X))\ \land\ \gamma\ge\sum_{X\in\mathcal P}(k-d_A^{\mathrm{out}}(X)).

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Defines global directed arc-connectivity augmentation, including the treatment of parallel arcs.

knowledge_statements.title: Rooted Directed Connectivity Augmentation

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\) be a finite digraph, let \(r\in V\), let \(F\subseteq V\times V\) be a set of candidate arcs, let \(c:F\to\mathbb{R}_{\ge 0}\), and let \(k\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 1}\). Equivalently, \[|\delta^-_{D+J}(X)|\ge k\qquad(\varnothing\ne X\subseteq V\setminus\{r\}).\] Inward augmentation requires \(k\) pairwise arc-disjoint directed \(v\)-to-\(r\) paths for every \(v\ne r\), equivalently the displayed condition after reversing every arc.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Find minimum-cost \(J\subseteq F\) satisfying \(|\delta^-_{D+J}(X)|\ge k\) for every nonempty \(X\subseteq V\setminus\{r\}\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Min–max theorem for augmenting a packing of rooted arborescences
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact weighted augmentation of a digraph from k to k+1 arc-disjoint arborescences rooted at a designated vertex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(D=(V,A)\) be a digraph, let \(r\in V\), and let \(k\in\mathbb Z_+\) be such that \(D\) contains \(k\) arc-disjoint \(r\)-arborescences. Let \(D'=(V,A')\) and \(l\in\mathbb Z_+^{A'}\). Then
\[
\min\left\{l(C): C\subseteq A',\ (V,A\cup C)\text{, with arc multiplicities, contains }k+1\text{ arc-disjoint }r\text{-arborescences}\right\}
\]
equals the maximum cardinality \(t\) of a family of nonempty sets \(U_1,\ldots,U_t\subseteq V\setminus\{r\}\) such that \(d_D^{\mathrm{in}}(U_j)=k\) for every \(j\), and each arc \(a\in A'\) enters at most \(l(a)\) of the sets \(U_j\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If a digraph already contains k arc-disjoint arborescences rooted at r, the minimum total l-cost of candidate arcs required to obtain k+1 such arborescences equals the largest size of a family of nonempty tight sets excluding r, each with exactly k entering arcs in the original digraph, for which every candidate arc a enters at most l(a) members of the family.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \min\{l(C):C\subseteq A',\ (V,A\cup C)\text{, with arc multiplicities, contains }k+1\text{ arc-disjoint }r\text{-arborescences}\}=\max\{t:\exists\,\varnothing\ne U_1,\ldots,U_t\subseteq V\setminus\{r\},\ d_D^{\mathrm{in}}(U_j)=k\ \forall j,\ |\{j:a\text{ enters }U_j\}|\le l(a)\ \forall a\in A'\}.

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Directed k-vertex-connectors, good pairs, and good collections
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definitions used by the directed vertex-connectivity augmentation min-max theorem; the extract also records the special k=1 equivalence and the ineffectiveness of parallel arcs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\) and \((V,B)\) be directed graphs. The arc set \(B\) is a \(k\)-vertex-connector for \(D\) if \((V,A\cup B)\) is \(k\)-vertex-connected. A pair \((X,Y)\) of subsets of \(V\) is good if \(X\ne\varnothing\), \(Y\ne\varnothing\), \(X\cap Y=\varnothing\), and \(D\) has no arc from \(X\) to \(Y\). A collection \(\mathcal F\) of good pairs is good if, for every two distinct \((X,Y),(X',Y')\in\mathcal F\), either \(X\cap X'=\varnothing\) or \(Y\cap Y'=\varnothing\). Parallel arcs do not improve vertex connectivity, and directed 1-vertex-connectors coincide with directed 1-arc-connectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A directed k-vertex-connector is an added arc set that makes the augmented digraph k-vertex-connected. A good pair consists of disjoint nonempty vertex sets with no arc from the first set to the second. A collection is good when any two pairs have disjoint first sets or disjoint second sets. Parallel arcs do not improve vertex connectivity, and the vertex- and arc-connector notions coincide when k equals one.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: B\text{ is a }k\text{-vertex-connector for }D\iff(V,A\cup B)\text{ is }k\text{-vertex-connected; good pairs and good collections are defined by the stated separation conditions.}

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Certificate for a bounded-size undirected 2-vertex-connector
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Necessary-and-sufficient feasibility certificate for a connector-size bound; N(U) retains its graph-neighborhood meaning from the source context.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a non-2-vertex-connected graph. Then \(G\) has a 2-vertex-connector of size at most \(\gamma\) if and only if both of the following hold: \(c(G-v)\le\gamma+1\) for every \(v\in V\), and \[\sum_{U\in\mathcal P}\left(2-|N(U)|\right)\le 2\gamma\] for every collection \(\mathcal P\) of pairwise disjoint nonempty subsets \(U\subseteq V\) satisfying \(|U|\le |V|-3\).

knowledge_statements.title: Source–Terminal Vertex-Connectivity Augmentation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Directed internal-vertex connectivity from designated sources to designated terminals.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D=(V,A)\) be a finite digraph, let \(S,T\subseteq V\) be nonempty, let \(F\subseteq V\times V\) be candidate arcs, let \(c:F\to\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}\), and let \(k\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge1}\). Source–terminal vertex-connectivity augmentation seeks \(J\subseteq F\) minimizing \(c(J)=\sum_{e\in J}c(e)\) such that every distinct \(s\in S\) and \(t\in T\) are joined in \(D+J=(V,A\cup J)\) by \(k\) internally vertex-disjoint directed \(s\)-to-\(t\) paths. Equivalently, for every such pair \((s,t)\), no set \(Z\subseteq V\setminus\{s,t\}\) with \(|Z|<k\) separates \(s\) from \(t\) in \(D+J\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Add minimum-cost candidate arcs so every distinct source-terminal pair has k internally vertex-disjoint directed paths from its source to its terminal.
assumptions_latex: \(D=(V,A)\) is finite and \(S,T\subseteq V\) are nonempty.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Find minimum-cost \(J\subseteq F\) giving \(k\) internally vertex-disjoint directed \(s\)-to-\(t\) paths for every distinct \((s,t)\in S\times T\).

knowledge_statements.title: Splitting-Off Augmentation Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reduction by admissible undirected or directed splitting-off at an auxiliary vertex.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a finite graph or digraph \(H\), a vertex \(v\), and required pairwise connectivities on \(V(H)\setminus\{v\}\). In the undirected case, choose incident edges \(uv,vw\), delete them, and add \(uw\). In the directed case, choose arcs \(uv,vw\), delete them, and add \(uw\). Accept the split only if every required connectivity between vertices distinct from \(v\) remains at least its prescribed value. Repeat admissible splits until no eligible pair remains or \(v\) becomes isolated; delete an isolated \(v\), solve the reduced augmentation instance, and reverse the recorded splits to reconstruct an augmentation of the original instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Repeatedly replace two edges or consecutive arcs through an auxiliary vertex by one link while preserving all required external connectivities.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is finite and the connectivity requirements exclude the split vertex \(v\).
Each chosen split is admissible for all prescribed terminal pairs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The procedure outputs a reduced instance together with a reversible log of connectivity-preserving splits.

knowledge_statements.title: Connectivity-Preserving Reductions
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Admissibility condition for reductions used in connectivity augmentation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H\) be a graph or digraph, let \(R(H)\) be the result of a proposed reduction, and let \(P\subseteq V(H)\times V(H)\) index terminal pairs unaffected by deleted auxiliary vertices. For a required connectivity function \(r:P\to\mathbb{Z}_{\ge 0}\), the reduction is connectivity-preserving precisely when \[\lambda_{R(H)}(s,t)\ge r(s,t)\qquad\text{for every }(s,t)\in P,\] where \(\lambda\) denotes the relevant edge-, arc-, or internally vertex-disjoint path connectivity. If \(H\) already meets the requirements, the stronger equality condition \(\lambda_{R(H)}(s,t)=\lambda_H(s,t)\) for every \((s,t)\in P\) is sufficient and preserves all pairwise connectivity values of interest.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A reduction is admissible when every relevant terminal-pair connectivity remains at least its required value.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) and \(R(H)\) have all terminals indexed by \(P\).
The same edge-, arc-, or vertex-connectivity convention defines both connectivity functions.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The reduction is admissible if \(\lambda_{R(H)}(s,t)\ge r(s,t)\) for all \((s,t)\in P\).

knowledge_statements.title: Reduced-Instance Reconstruction
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reverse lifting of a reduced augmentation through recorded reductions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(I_0,I_1,\ldots,I_m\) be augmentation instances with recorded reductions \(R_i:I_{i-1}\to I_i\). Assume each reduction has a lifting map \(L_i\) such that every feasible augmentation \(J_i\) of \(I_i\) is mapped to a feasible augmentation \(L_i(J_i)\) of \(I_{i-1}\), with \(c(L_i(J_i))\le c(J_i)+\alpha_i\). Solve \(I_m\) to obtain \(J_m\), then set \[J_{i-1}=L_i(J_i)\qquad(i=m,m-1,\ldots,1).\] Output \(J_0\). The reconstruction is exact when every \(\alpha_i=0\) and each lifting map preserves the objective value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Lift a reduced solution by undoing recorded reductions in reverse order; feasibility is preserved and lifting overhead accumulates additively.
assumptions_latex: Each \(L_i\) maps feasible augmentations of \(I_i\) to feasible augmentations of \(I_{i-1}\).
Each lifting step has certified cost overhead at most \(\alpha_i\ge 0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output \(J_0\) is feasible and satisfies \(c(J_0)\le c(J_m)+\sum_{i=1}^{m}\alpha_i\).

notation.meaning: Instance after i reductions.
Lifting map reversing reduction i.

knowledge_statements.title: Cactus Cut Representations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cactus encoding of an undirected graph's global minimum cuts.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a finite connected undirected graph, and let \(\mathcal{M}\) be the family of shores of its global minimum cuts. There exist a cactus \(K\) and a map \(\phi:V\to V(K)\) such that \(\mathcal{M}\) consists exactly of the inverse images under \(\phi\) of shores obtained either by deleting one bridge of \(K\) or by deleting two edges belonging to a common cycle of \(K\). Thus every \(X\in\mathcal{M}\) has the form \(X=\phi^{-1}(W)\) for a component vertex set \(W\subset V(K)\) produced by an allowed deletion, and every such shore of \(K\) pulls back to a global minimum-cut shore of \(G\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: All global minimum-cut shores of a finite connected undirected graph can be encoded by bridge deletions or two-edge deletions on cycles of a cactus.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is a finite connected undirected graph.
\(\mathcal{M}\) is the family of shores of global minimum cuts of \(G\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: There exist a cactus \(K\) and map \(\phi:V\to V(K)\) encoding exactly \(\mathcal{M}\) through the stated deletions.

knowledge_statements.title: Block Decomposition Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Block-cut decomposition at articulation vertices of an undirected graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a finite connected undirected graph \(G=(V,E)\). Run depth-first search, recording discovery times and low-link values. Declare a nonroot vertex \(v\) an articulation vertex when some DFS child \(w\) satisfies \(\operatorname{low}(w)\ge\operatorname{disc}(v)\); declare the root an articulation vertex when it has at least two DFS children. Pop edges from the DFS edge stack at each such event to form maximal blocks having no articulation vertex internally. Output the bipartite block-cut graph whose nodes are the blocks and articulation vertices, with incidence given by containment. This graph is a tree and exposes subinstances attached through single articulation vertices.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A DFS partitions a connected graph into maximal blocks and articulation vertices, producing a block-cut tree for separable processing.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is a finite connected undirected graph.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The algorithm outputs all maximal blocks, all articulation vertices, and their block-cut tree.

notation.meaning: DFS discovery time of v.
Earliest discovery time reachable from v's DFS subtree by at most one back edge.

knowledge_statements.title: Component-Decomposition Methods
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Recursive decomposition into maximal undirected k-edge-connected vertex classes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a finite undirected graph \(G=(V,E)\) and an integer \(k\in\mathbb{Z}_{\ge1}\). For a current nonempty set \(U\subseteq V\), if \(\lambda_G(s,t)\ge k\) for every distinct \(s,t\in U\), output \(U\). Otherwise choose \(s,t\in U\) with \(\lambda_G(s,t)<k\), compute an \(s\)-\(t\) cut \((X,V\setminus X)\) of size less than \(k\), and recurse on the two nonempty sets \(U\cap X\) and \(U\setminus X\). Starting with \(U=V\), the output sets are the equivalence classes of \[u\sim_k v\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad u=v\ \text{ or }\ \lambda_G(u,v)\ge k.\] They are exactly the maximal vertex sets whose distinct members have pairwise edge-connectivity at least \(k\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Recursively intersect the current vertex set with the shores of cuts smaller than k to obtain the maximal classes whose vertices are pairwise k-edge-connected.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output partitions \(V\) into the equivalence classes of \(\sim_k\).

notation.meaning: Minimum size of an undirected u-v edge cut.
Pairwise k-edge-connectivity relation.

Then an \(r\)-edge-connector \(F\) satisfying \(\deg_F(v)=x_v\) for every \(v\in V\) exists if and only if \(x(V)\) is even and \[x(U)+d_E(U)\ge r(u,v)\] for every \(U\subseteq V\), \(u\in U\), and \(v\in V\setminus U\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Provided no connected component has total prescribed added degree one, an exact-degree r-edge-connector exists exactly when the total prescribed degree is even and every separating cut has sufficient existing and prescribed incidence for each separated pair's demand.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists F:\ F\text{ is an }r\text{-edge-connector and }\deg_F(v)=x_v\ \forall v\in V\iff x(V)\text{ is even and }x(U)+d_E(U)\ge r(u,v)\ \forall U\subseteq V,\ u\in U,\ v\notin U

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Degree-bounded cardinality criterion for a k-edge-connector
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes feasibility of undirected k-edge-connectivity augmentation subject to a cardinality limit and lower and upper added-degree bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be an undirected graph, let \(k,\gamma\in\mathbb Z_+\) with \(k\ge2\), and let \(l,u\in\mathbb Z_+^V\) with \(l\le u\). Then \(G\) has a \(k\)-edge-connector \(F\) satisfying \(|F|\le\gamma\) and \(l(v)\le\deg_F(v)\le u(v)\) for every \(v\in V\) if and only if \(2\gamma\le u(V)\), \(k-d_E(U)\le u(U)\) for every nonempty proper subset \(U\subset V\), and \[2\gamma\ge l\!\left(V\setminus\bigcup\mathcal P\right)+\sum_{U\in\mathcal P}\left(k-d_E(U)\right)\] for every collection \(\mathcal P\) of pairwise disjoint nonempty proper subsets of \(V\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A k-edge-connector meeting the cardinality and added-degree bounds exists exactly when the stated total upper-degree, cut upper-degree, and disjoint-family inequalities hold.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \exists F:\ |F|\le\gamma,\ l(v)\le\deg_F(v)\le u(v)\ \forall v\in V\iff 2\gamma\le u(V),\ k-d_E(U)\le u(U)\ \forall\varnothing\ne U\subsetneq V,\ \text{and }2\gamma\ge l(V\setminus\bigcup\mathcal P)+\sum_{U\in\mathcal P}(k-d_E(U))\ \forall\mathcal P

children.top_down_role: Augmentation when only designated candidate links are available.

assumptions_latex: \(L\subseteq\binom{V}{2}\) is the designated set of candidate link types, and \(k\in\mathbb Z_{\ge1}\).
No link type outside \(L\) may be added.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Restricted-link feasibility is exactly the existence of a nonnegative integral multiplicity vector supported on \(L\) that covers every residual cut deficit.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A restricted-link augmentation is a vector \(x\in\mathbb Z_+^L\), with zero multiplicity assigned to every link type outside \(L\). It is feasible for target \(k\) if and only if \[d_G(X)+\sum_{e\in\delta_L(X)}x_e\ge k\quad\text{for every }\varnothing\ne X\subsetneq V.\] In particular, a set \(X\) with \(d_G(X)<k\) and \(\delta_L(X)=\varnothing\) is an infeasibility certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A restricted-link augmentation uses only designated link types and is feasible exactly when their integral multiplicities cover every deficient cut.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(L=\binom{V}{2}\setminus E\). A simple-graph \(k\)-edge-connectivity augmentation is a set \(F\subseteq L\) such that \((V,E\cup F)\) is \(k\)-edge-connected. Equivalently, the incidence vector \(x\in\{0,1\}^L\) of \(F\) satisfies \[\sum_{e\in\delta_L(X)}x_e\ge\max\{0,k-d_G(X)\}\quad\text{for every }\varnothing\ne X\subsetneq V.\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A simple-graph augmentation selects each nonedge at most once and makes the resulting simple graph k-edge-connected.

\(k\in\mathbb Z_{\ge1}\), and each \(e\in L\) has a capacity \(u_e\in\mathbb Z_{\ge0}\).

knowledge_statements.statement_title: Complexity regimes of connectivity augmentation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classifies the four basic directed/undirected and arc-or-edge/vertex connectivity-augmentation variants.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the minimum-cardinality augmentation problem, directed $k$-arc-connectivity, undirected $k$-edge-connectivity, and directed $k$-vertex-connectivity admit min--max relations and polynomial-time algorithms. Undirected $k$-vertex-connectivity augmentation is polynomial-time solvable for each fixed $k$, while its complexity when $k$ is part of the input is open.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Directed arc-, undirected edge-, and directed vertex-connectivity augmentation have min-max characterizations and polynomial-time algorithms. Undirected vertex-connectivity augmentation is polynomial-time solvable for fixed k, but its complexity for unrestricted k is open.
assumptions_latex: \text{The objective is to add a minimum number of edges or arcs to attain }k\text{-connectivity.}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \begin{aligned}&\text{The directed arc, undirected edge, and directed vertex variants have min--max relations and polynomial-time algorithms;}\\&\text{the undirected vertex variant is polynomial-time solvable for fixed }k,\text{ while the general-}k\text{ complexity is open.}\end{aligned}

children.top_down_role: Structural and algorithmic differences between edge and vertex failure models.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The family \(H_m\) satisfies \(\lambda(H_m)=m\) and \(\kappa(H_m)=1\), so arbitrarily large edge connectivity does not imply vertex connectivity greater than one.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(m\ge2\), let \(H_m\) be the simple graph obtained from two vertex-disjoint copies of \(K_{m+1}\) by identifying one vertex of the first copy with one vertex of the second. Then \[\lambda(H_m)=m\qquad\text{and}\qquad\kappa(H_m)=1.\] Thus a family can have unbounded edge connectivity while retaining a one-vertex separator, so ordinary edge-cut constraints do not characterize vertex connectivity.

knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The unique minimum-cardinality augmentation is \(\{ad\}\), whereas the unique minimum-cost augmentation is \(\{ac,bd\}\).

Cost of the expensive closing link
Cost of a selected link set

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For the specified path, candidate links, and costs, both \(F_1=\{ad\}\) and \(F_2=\{ac,bd\}\) yield \(2\)-edge-connected augmented graphs. The set \(F_1\) is the unique feasible one-link augmentation, so it is the unique minimum-cardinality solution. Since \(c(F_1)=M>2=c(F_2)\), the set \(F_2\) is the unique minimum-cost solution. Hence minimum cardinality and minimum nonuniform cost select different augmentations on this instance.

children.title: Global versus Subset-Connectivity Boundary
children.top_down_role: The transition from uniform global connectivity to terminal-pair requirements.

assumptions_latex: Each unordered terminal pair \(s,t\) has an integral requirement \(r_{st}\ge0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Pairwise edge-connectivity requirements are equivalent to nonuniform cut bounds \(d_H(X)\ge R(X)\); global connectivity is their constant-demand special case.

notation.meaning: Maximum requirement separated by cut X
Size of the edge boundary of X in H

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cut-demand transition from uniform global edge connectivity to pair-specific terminal connectivity.

source_refs.locator: 9.2 Global k-edge-connection p. 297

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define \(R(X)=\max\{r_{st}:|\{s,t\}\cap X|=1\}\), taking the maximum of an empty set as zero. By the edge form of Menger's theorem, \(H\) contains at least \(r_{st}\) edge-disjoint \(s\)-\(t\) paths for every pair if and only if \[d_H(X)\ge R(X)\qquad\text{for every }\varnothing\ne X\subsetneq V.\] Global \(k\)-edge-connectivity is the special case \(r_{st}=k\) for all distinct \(s,t\), when \(R(X)=k\) on every nontrivial cut. Nonuniform terminal requirements therefore replace one scalar cut threshold by a cut-dependent demand function.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Pair-specific terminal connectivity uses the maximum separated-pair demand on each cut; uniform global connectivity is the constant-demand special case.

knowledge_statements.title: Tree Augmentation Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Characterizes edge-connectivity augmentation on a tree and identifies why the path-cover formulation is tree-specific.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Let \(T=(V,E_T)\) be a finite tree and let \(L\subseteq \binom{V}{2}\setminus E_T\) be candidate links. For each \(\ell=uv\in L\), let \(P_T(\ell)\) denote the unique \(u\)-to-\(v\) path in \(T\). A set \(F\subseteq L\) makes \(T+F\) two-edge-connected if and only if
\[
\bigcup_{\ell\in F}E(P_T(\ell))=E_T,
\]
equivalently, every cut induced by deleting one tree edge is crossed by a link in \(F\). The tree assumption is essential to this exact path-cover characterization: for the cyclic backbone \(G=C_3\), the graph \(G\) is already two-edge-connected with \(F=\varnothing\), although no backbone edge is covered by a selected link path.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Tree augmentation is exactly a covering problem for unique tree paths. This formulation ceases to characterize feasibility on cyclic backbones, which may already be two-edge-connected without covering their edges.
assumptions_latex: \(L\subseteq \binom{V}{2}\setminus E_T\) is a finite set of candidate augmentation edges.
\(F\subseteq L\) is the selected augmentation set.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(T+F\) is two-edge-connected exactly when every edge of \(T\) lies on \(P_T(\ell)\) for some \(\ell\in F\); this equivalence does not extend unchanged to non-tree backbones, as witnessed by \(C_3\) with \(F=\varnothing\).

notation.meaning: The unique path between vertices u and v in the tree T.
The graph with vertex set V and edge set consisting of the tree edges and selected links.
The undirected cycle on three vertices.
